{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_0852c6f7e19a4a43b6be0e49","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Deliver a user's conversation list over the WebSocket protocol\n2\t\n3\tIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#144\n4\tLabels: type:feature, size:M, area:api, area:compliance, epic:extension-points\n5\t\n6\tPart of #35\n7\t\n8\t## Why\n9\t\n10\t#143 gives a consumer `store.listFor(userId)`.\n11\tIt does not give a **client** anything: the browser holding the socket cannot reach the store, so\n12\tevery consumer that wants a history sidebar has to stand up its own authenticated HTTP route over\n13\tthe same data the engine already authenticated on the upgrade. That is a second authorisation\n14\tpath to the same personal data, written once per consumer, each one able to get the ownership\n15\tcheck wrong in its own way — the exact failure #45 went out of its way to avoid for resume.\n16\t\n17\tA consumer may have no such route to extend: an engine deployment behind an api with a session\n18\tstore and no conversation endpoints of its own has nothing to add this to. The engine already knows who is connected and already\n19\treplays a conversation on resume; answering \"which conversations do I have\" over the same socket\n20\tis the smaller surface.\n21\t\n22\t## What to do\n23\t\n24\t- `src/types/messages.ts`, additive only:\n25\t  - `ListConversationsMessage {type: 'list_conversations'; limit?: number; before?: string}` into\n26\t    `IncomingMessage`. There is no user id field, and that is the point: the list is always the\n27\t    connection's authenticated user's.\n28\t  - `ConversationListMessage {type: 'conversation_list'; conversations: ConversationSummary[]}`\n29\t    into `OutgoingMessage`, where `ConversationSummary` is `SessionSummary` with its two times as\n30\t    ISO strings — `Date` does not survive `JSON.stringify` as a `Date`, and the protocol types\n31\t    describe what goes on the wire.\n32\t- `validation.ts`: a `list_conversations` case — `limit`, when present, an integer 1–200;\n33\t  `before`, when present, a string `Date.parse` accepts. Anything else is `INVALID_MESSAGE`, as\n34\t  the two existing cases do it.\n35\t- Handling: `createMessageHandler` takes the session store and the new options alongside the\n36\t  orchestrator (`createServer` already holds both), and answers `list_conversations` on the\n37\t  non-locked path beside `ping` — a history request is not a turn and must not queue behind a\n38\t  streaming answer.\n39\t- The user id comes from `ws.userId`, never from the frame. Add the regression:\n40\t  a frame carrying an extra `userId` of another user is answered with the connecting user's own\n41\t  list.\n42\t- Opt-in: `HalEngineConfig.transport.history?: {enabled: boolean}`, default off, threaded through\n43\t  `createServer`'s options like `resume`. With it off, `list_conversations` is answered with an\n44\t  `error` frame and no list.\n45\t- A store that implements no `listFor` is answered with an `error`, not an empty list: a client\n46\t  that renders \"no conversations\" for a user who has several is a worse answer than one that\n47\t  renders a failure. `ErrorCodes` gains one code for both cases (`UNSUPPORTED`), additive.\n48\t- Picking a conversation needs nothing new: the client reconnects with `?sessionId=<id>`, which\n49\t  #45 already ships with the ownership check and the replay. No in-band switch frame, no second\n50\t  replay path.\n51\t- Specs and docs: extend `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md` (the two frames, their\n52\t  field tables, the authorisation rule) and the conversation-list spec; add § Conversation list\n53\t  to `docs/getting-started.md` by editing `example/full-config.ts` and running `npm run docs:fix`\n54\t  — that listing sits under `<!-- doc-block: example/full-config.ts#full-config -->` and\n55\t  `npm run docs:check` fails a hand-edited block.\n56\t\n57\t## Decisions\n58\t\n59\t- **A frame, not a REST route.** The REST chat routes are demo-only and are not where a consumer is meant to build. The WebSocket is where the caller is\n60\t  already authenticated, once per connection, by the consumer's own `wsAuth`.\n61\t- **Its own opt-in flag, separate from `resume`.** Resume hands a client back a conversation it\n62\t  was already in; a list tells it what else the user has. A deployer who turned on resume did not\n63\t  thereby agree to the second disclosure, and a config that conflates them cannot be audited.\n64\t- **Answered off the per-session lock.** `PerSessionLock` serialises turns (#47). A list request\n65\t  that queued behind a two-minute streaming answer would look broken, and it mutates nothing.\n66\t- **An error, not an empty list, when it cannot be answered.** See above; silence that looks like\n67\t  data is the one failure mode a history view cannot recover from.\n68\t- **Answered when asked, never pushed.** No `conversation_list` arrives unsolicited: a client\n69\t  that just started a conversation knows, and a push would need a fan-out across the sockets a\n70\t  resumed session can be open on.\n71\t- **The frame is accepted by `validateMessage` whether or not the feature is on**, and the\n72\t  handler is what refuses it. This was written before\n92\t      #143's review found that paging on a timestamp alone drops a conversation whenever two\n93\t      share an activity time, so the store's cursor became a composite that accepts an ISO\n94\t      string; a `Date` cannot carry the tie-break. Built as originally written, the transport would have reintroduced the defect the store\n137\t   had just been fixed for.\n138\t2. **`messages.ts` gains four interfaces, not two** — the two frames plus the two payload types\n139\t   they describe.\n140\t3. **`StoreCannotList` is new public surface**, beyond what this issue specified: without it a\n141\t   permanent store misconfiguration cannot be told from a transient failure, in either the client\n142\t   frame or the log.\n143\t\n144\tTwo decisions the criteria did not anticipate:\n145\t\n146\t- **`transport.history` without `transport.resume` is useless, and now says so.** `?sessionId=` is\n147\t  read only when resume is enabled, so a list whose rows cannot be opened is a deployment slip:\n148\t  the engine warns at startup and the documentation says so where it tells a client to reconnect\n149\t  with a row's id. This was written before\n      #143's review found that paging on a timestamp alone drops a conversation whenever two\n      share an activity time, so the store's cursor became a composite that accepts an ISO\n      string; a `Date` cannot carry the tie-break. The handler passes `{limit, before}` with\n      both possibly `undefined` rather than omitting the argument, which is the same call\n- [ ] With `history` absent, the same frame is answered with one `error` frame whose code is\n      `UNSUPPORTED` and no `conversation_list`\n- [ ] With `history: {enabled: true}` against a store implementing no `listFor`, the answer is\n      the same `error` frame, and `grep` shows no code path that sends `conversations: []`\n- [ ] A `listFor` that rejects is answered with one `error` frame whose code is `SERVER_ERROR`\n      and whose message carries no store detail, the socket stays open, and the failure is\n      logged with the session id and no user content. **Added during the build:** a store throwing\n      the new exported `StoreCannotList` is answered `UNSUPPORTED` instead, so an injected\n      collection without a `find` reads as the misconfiguration it is rather than a database\n      that failed\n- [ ] A `list_conversations` sent while a `user_message` is streaming on the same session is\n      answered before that turn's `stream_end` — it does not wait on the lock\n- [ ] A client that takes an id from a `conversation_list` and reconnects with `?sessionId=<id>`\n      receives `resumed: true` and that conversation's replay, with no new transport code: the\n      test exercises the existing #45 path end to end\n- [ ] `ConnectedMessage` is unchanged by this issue\n- [ ] **GDPR.** The protocol spec states that `conversation_list` carries one authenticated\n      user's own conversation metadata and no conversation content, that the user id is taken\n      from the connection and never from the frame, and that `transport.history` is the\n      deployer's decision to make a user's history reachable from the client; `SessionResumeOptions`'\n      retention note is mirrored on the new options type, pointing at #41\n- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` carries an entry under `## [Unreleased]` written for somebody installing the\n      package\n- [ ] The `docs/getting-started.md` change is made in `example/full-config.ts` and the doc\n      regenerated with `npm run docs:fix`, not typed into the markdown\n- [ ] Spec statements carry trailing `([validated by: ...](...#Lnn))` citations, `Status` rows\n      match coverage, and `npm run check:spec-links`, `npm run check:spec-status` and\n      `npm run spec:names` pass\n- [ ] The version bump is MINOR — new optional config, two additive protocol frames, one new\n      error code — and the PR body says so; no migration guide is owed\n- [ ] `npm run verify` passes and the coverage floors for the touched groups hold or rise\n\n## Amendments\n\nThree things changed between writing this issue and building it, each marked in the criterion it\naffects:\n\n1. **`before` is a cursor, not a timestamp.** #143's review found that paging on `updatedAt` alone\n   silently drops a conversation when two share an activity time. The store's cursor became\n   `{updatedAt, sessionId}`, so the frame carries both halves and the validator refuses one half\n   alone. Built as originally written, the transport would have reintroduced the defect the store\n   had just been fixed for.\n2. **`messages.ts` gains four interfaces, not two** — the two frames plus the two payload types\n   they describe.\n3. **`StoreCannotList` is new public surface**, beyond what this issue specified: without it a\n   permanent store misconfiguration cannot be told from a transient failure, in either the client\n   frame or the log.\n\nTwo decisions the criteria did not anticipate:\n\n- **`transport.history` without `transport.resume` is useless, and now says so.** `?sessionId=` is\n  read only when resume is enabled, so a list whose rows cannot be opened is a deployment slip:\n  the engine warns at startup and the documentation says so where it tells a client to reconnect\n  with a row's id. Refusing to start was considered and rejected as too blunt for a library.\n- **The conversation the connection is in is listed like any other**, so a fresh connect sees a row\n  of its own holding no entries. Filtering it out was rejected: it is a real conversation the user\n  is in, and it is their newest the moment they send anything.\n\n## Tech notes\n\nDepends on #143: without `listFor` there is\nnothing to send.\n\nKey paths: `src/types/messages.ts`, `src/types/session.ts` (`ErrorCodes`),\n`src/transport/ws/{validation,messageHandler,sender}.ts`, `src/transport/createServer.ts`,\n`src/config.ts`, `example/full-config.ts`, `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md`.\n\nOut of scope: a preview or title on the summaries (its own issue); deleting a conversation from\nthe client, which would put an erasure primitive on the wire and needs its own authorisation\ndecision; paging state held server-side — the client pages with `before`; an operator view of\nanother user's conversations, which is an authorisation question of its own; and live sync between open tabs,\nwhich #124 ruled out.\n\nRefs #143, #145, #41, #45, #47, #124\n\n\n\n\n","numLines":174,"startLine":1,"totalLines":174}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_0852c6f7e19a4a43b6be0e49","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

askAfterConnect(withoutList, {type: 'list_sessions'});\n    const failed = await askAfterConnect(failingList, {type: 'list_sessions'});\n\n    expect({\n      unimplemented: unimplemented.frames,\n      failed: failed.frames.map(frame => ({type: frame.type, code: frame.code})),\n      logged: logLines.filter(line => line.level === 'error' && line.category === 'ws'),\n    }).toEqual({\n      unimplemented: [{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}],\n      failed: [{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}],\n      logged: [\n        {\n          level: 'error',\n          category: 'ws',\n          message: expect.any(String),\n          fields: expect.objectContaining({userId: 'u1', error: 'database offline'}),\n        },\n      ],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor', async () => {\n    const inner = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    let calls = 0;\n    const store: SessionStore = {\n      ...delegatingTo(inner),\n      listFor: () => {\n        calls += 1;\n        return [];\n      },\n    };\n    const url = await startEngine(store);\n    const badFrames = [\n      {type: 'list_sessions', limit: 'ten'},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', limit: -1},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', limit: 1.5},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: 'not-an-object'},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: {updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', sessionId: ''}},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: {updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', sessionId: 'a'.repeat(129)}},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: {updatedAt: 'not-a-date', sessionId: 's1'}},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: {updatedAt: true, sessionId: 's1'}},\n    ];\n\n    const codes: Array<string | undefined> = [];\n    for (const bad of badFrames) {\n      const {frames} = await askAfterConnect(url, bad);\n      codes.push(frames[0]?.code);\n    }\n    const {frames: accepted} = await askAfterConnect(url, {type: 'list_sessions'});\n\n    expect({codes, accepted, calls}).toEqual({\n      codes: Array(badFrames.length).fill('INVALID_MESSAGE'),\n      accepted: [{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}],\n      calls: 1,\n    });\n  });\n});\n","numLines":199,"startLine":1,"totalLines":199}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_e76032e759c24dd58bb26ac0","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

SessionListMessage;\n \n export {ErrorCodes} from './session.js';\n=== spec file full ===\n# Conversation List\n\n| Field  | Value                 |\n| ------ | --------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#143 |\n| Status | Shipped               |\n\nResume gets a client back into one conversation: the id it names, or the user's most recently active one. Neither tells it which conversations exist, and every other member of `SessionStore` answers about a session the caller can already name, so a consumer wanting to offer a conversation list had to query the collection behind the engine's back, against a document shape and a key the engine owns. `listFor` answers the list instead, as summaries rather than sessions. **GDPR.** A summary is personal data — that a user held a conversation, and when — so it carries no conversation content, it is filtered to one user by the query rather than in application code afterwards, and the retention bound stays the consumer's, through the store's `maxAgeMs` and erasure methods and re-cinq/HALEngine#41.\n\n## The summary\n\n- A summary is `sessionId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `entryCount`, and nothing else: neither the conversation's entries nor its credentials, so a list can never hand over either, even for a session created with credentials ([validated by: carries only its four fields, so a list can never hand over a conversation or a credential](../../src/infrastructure/stores/sessionStoreListSignature.test.ts#L22)).\n- `listFor` is optional, like `latestFor` and `lookup` before it: a store written against the five original members still satisfies the interface, and both shipped stores implement it ([validated by: leaves a store with only the five original members satisfying the interface beside both shipped ones](../../src/infrastructure/stores/sessionStoreListSignature.test.ts#L11)).\n\n## The order a list answers in\n\n- Summaries come back most recent activity first ([validated by: answers newest activity first, headed by the very session latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L27)).\n- The first summary is the session `latestFor` returns, because both read the same activity ([validated by: answers newest activity first, headed by the very session latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L27)).\n- The order is total rather than merely sorted: two conversations last active in the same millisecond are ordered by session id, the larger first, which is what lets a page resume without dropping one of them ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on activity rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L141)).\n- In `InMemorySessionStore` that tie-break is the list's alone: `latestFor` breaks the same tie by creation order, so for two tied conversations the head of the list and the session a resume rejoins can differ ([validated by: breaks a tie on activity by session id, where latestFor takes the session created later](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L42)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` answers in order of `updatedAt`, which each `save` moves forward, and its first summary is the session its own `latestFor` returns ([validated by: answers the user's conversations newest saved first, headed by the one latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L31)).\n- It breaks a tie by `_id` in both members, so there the head of the list is the session a resume rejoins even when every conversation shares an `updatedAt` ([validated by: heads the list with the session latestFor returns even when every conversation shares an updatedAt](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L161)).\n\n## What a summary reports\n\n- `InMemorySessionStore` reports the moment `create` was called, the newest entry time as the activity, and the conversation's entry count ([validated by: reports a creation time, the newest activity and the entry count of each conversation](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L53)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` reports the document's `createdAt`, the `updatedAt` its last save wrote, and the counter written beside the entries ([validated by: reports the creation time, the last save and the entry count of each conversation](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L49)).\n- That counter is what a save writes, so a list never reads a conversation to count one ([validated by: counts a conversation from the field a save writes beside the entries](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L95)).\n- A document written before the counter existed reads as a conversation of no entries rather than failing the list, which is what the backlog documented in `docs/session-stores.md` is for ([validated by: reads a conversation saved before the counter existed as one of no entries, rather than failing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L79)).\n\n## Whose conversations\n\n- A list holds only the asking user's conversations: another user's never appear, and a user with none gets an empty list ([validated by: omits a conversation that aged out and another user's, and answers nothing for a user with none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L65)).\n- `InMemorySessionStore` omits a conversation that has aged out, as `latestFor` does ([validated by: omits a conversation that aged out and another user's, and answers nothing for a user with none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L65)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` filters on the user in the database, sorts on `{updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` — the `{userId: 1, updatedAt: -1}` index `latestFor` already needs serves its leading keys — and asks for a projection that leaves the entries behind ([validated by: asks the database to filter on the user, sort on the index with the id behind it, and never for the entries](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L108)).\n- It answers from that projection alone, so a collection that never returns an entry still lists conversations — the conversation does not leave the database to be listed ([validated by: answers from a projection alone, so a collection that never returns entries still lists conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L181)).\n\n## Paging\n\n- `limit` takes that many of the newest, and `before` resumes after a row, so a client pages by passing back the last summary it saw — `SessionCursor` is `updatedAt` and `sessionId`, which a `SessionSummary` already satisfies ([validated by: pages down the same order: a limit takes the newest, and before takes what is older than it](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L78)).\n- Paging walks every conversation exactly once even when all of them share an activity time, because the cursor carries the session id the order breaks ties on: a tie cannot fall between two pages and be skipped ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on activity rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L141)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` pages the same way ([validated by: pages with before and a limit, down the same newest-first order](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L62)).\n- It walks a tie exactly once too, through the same cursor ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on updatedAt rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L127)).\n- A list is at most 200 summaries however many are asked for, and 50 when none is asked for, so no caller can ask for an unbounded page ([validated by: answers at most two hundred conversations however many are asked for, and fifty when none is](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L94)).\n- That limit bounds the rows answered, not the rows the database reads to answer them: on `MongoSessionStore` the work is bounded by the `{userId: 1, updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` index `docs/session-stores.md` prescribes, and under the two-key form Mongo sorts the user's whole history before applying the limit ([validated by: needs the three-key index to answer without sorting the whole history, which the two-key form does not](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L192)).\n- A fractional limit is floored rather than refused, since a slip in a limit is not a reason to deny a user their history ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n- A negative limit, and one that is not a usable number, are read as no limit given at all rather than as a limit of none: handing a user an empty history for a typo is the worse reading ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n- Only a limit of exactly `0` answers no conversations ([validated by: answers nothing only for a limit of exactly none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L116)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` answers a limit of `0` without querying, because MongoDB reads `limit: 0` as no limit at all and would otherwise answer with every conversation the filter matches ([validated by: answers a limit of none without asking the database, which reads a limit of zero as no limit at all](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L143)).\n\n## The two shipped stores answer one order\n\n- `InMemorySessionStore` and `MongoSessionStore` list the same conversations in the same order, so a consumer swapping one for the other sees the same conversation list ([validated by: answer the same order for conversations whose activity differs](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L43)).\n- They break a tie on activity the same way, by session id ([validated by: break a tie on activity the same way, by session id](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L52)).\n- They page identically through the documented call, `listFor(userId, {limit, before: rows.at(-1)})`, a page at a time until a page comes back empty ([validated by: page the same way through the documented call, two rows at a time from the last row seen](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L61)).\n\n## A cursor the caller can actually hold\n\n- A cursor's `updatedAt` may be a `Date`, an ISO string or an epoch number, so a summary that went through JSON on its way to a client and back still pages ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, and refuses one carrying no usable moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` reads such a cursor as a date before it queries, since a string compares against no stored BSON date and would quietly match none of them ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, where a string would have matched no stored date](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L150)).\n- A cursor carrying no usable moment is refused with an error naming it, rather than read as no cursor at all, which would answer the first page again and repeat rows a client has already shown ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, and refuses one carrying no usable moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n\n## A collection that cannot list\n\n- `find` is optional on `CollectionLike`, so an adapter written before conversation lists existed still satisfies the port ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n- A store built on a collection without it refuses to list, rather than reporting that the user has no conversations ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n\n## When the store cannot answer\n\n- A store whose collection fails rejects rather than answering a partial or empty list: what to show a user who may have conversations is the caller's decision, and an empty history is not a safe guess ([validated by: rejects rather than answering a partial list when the collection fails](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L225)).\n\n## Over the WebSocket protocol\n\n- A client sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit?, before?}` and receives `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` for the socket's authenticated user, with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings and any client-supplied `userId` ignored ([validated by: answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L93)).\n- A store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}`, and a throwing `listFor` logs an error on the `ws` category and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L134)).\n- The validator accepts an optional non-negative integer `limit` and an optional `before` cursor whose `sessionId` is 1–128 bound stays the consumer's, through the store's `maxAgeMs` and erasure methods and re-cinq/HALEngine#41.\n\n## The summary\n\n- A summary is `sessionId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `entryCount`, and nothing else: neither the conversation's entries nor its credentials, so a list can never hand over either, even for a session created with credentials ([validated by: carries only its four fields, so a list can never hand over a conversation or a credential](../../src/infrastructure/stores/sessionStoreListSignature.test.ts#L22)).\n- `listFor` is optional, like `latestFor` and `lookup` before it: a store written against the five original members still satisfies the interface, and both shipped stores implement it ([validated by: leaves a store with only the five original members satisfying the interface beside both shipped ones](../../src/infrastructure/stores/sessionStoreListSignature.test.ts#L11)).\n\n## The order a list answers in\n\n- Summaries come back most recent activity first ([validated by: answers newest activity first, headed by the very session latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L27)).\n- The first summary is the session `latestFor` returns, because both read the same activity ([validated by: answers newest activity first, headed by the very session latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L27)).\n- The order is total rather than merely sorted: two conversations last active in the same millisecond are ordered by session id, the larger first, which is what lets a page resume without dropping one of them ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on activity rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L141)).\n- In `InMemorySessionStore` that tie-break is the list's alone: `latestFor` breaks the same tie by creation order, so for two tied conversations the head of the list and the session a resume rejoins can differ ([validated by: breaks a tie on activity by session id, where latestFor takes the session created later](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L42)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` answers in order of `updatedAt`, which each `save` moves forward, and its first summary is the session its own `latestFor` returns ([validated by: answers the user's conversations newest saved first, headed by the one latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L31)).\n- It breaks a tie by `_id` in both members, so there the head of the list is the session a resume rejoins even when every conversation shares an `updatedAt` ([validated by: heads the list with the session latestFor returns even when every conversation shares an updatedAt](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L161)).\n\n## What a summary reports\n\n- `InMemorySessionStore` reports the moment `create` was called, the newest entry time as the activity, and the conversation's entry count ([validated by: reports a creation time, the newest activity and the entry count of each conversation](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L53)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` reports the document's `createdAt`, the `updatedAt` its last save wrote, and the counter written beside the entries ([validated by: reports the creation time, the last save and the entry count of each conversation](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L49)).\n- That counter is what a save writes, so a list never reads a conversation to count one ([validated by: counts a conversation from the field a save writes beside the entries](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L95)).\n- A document written before the counter existed reads as a conversation of no entries rather than failing the list, which is what the backlog documented in `docs/session-stores.md` is for ([validated by: reads a conversation saved before the counter existed as one of no entries, rather than failing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L79)).\n\n## Whose conversations\n\n- A list holds only the asking user's conversations: another user's never appear, and a user with none gets an empty list ([validated by: omits a conversation that aged out and another user's, and answers nothing for a user with none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L65)).\n- `InMemorySessionStore` omits a conversation that has aged out, as `latestFor` does ([validated by: omits a conversation that aged out and another user's, and answers nothing for a user with none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L65)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` filters on the user in the database, sorts on `{updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` — the `{userId: 1, updatedAt: -1}` index `latestFor` already needs serves its leading keys — and asks for a projection that leaves the entries behind ([validated by: asks the database to filter on the user, sort on the index with the id behind it, and never for the entries](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L108)).\n- It answers from that projection alone, so a collection that never returns an entry still lists conversations — the conversation does not leave the database to be listed ([validated by: answers from a projection alone, so a collection that never returns entries still lists conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L181)).\n\n## Paging\n\n- `limit` takes that many of the newest, and `before` resumes after a row, so a client pages by passing back the last summary it saw — `SessionCursor` is `updatedAt` and `sessionId`, which a `SessionSummary` already satisfies ([validated by: pages down the same order: a limit takes the newest, and before takes what is older than it](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L78)).\n- Paging walks every conversation exactly once even when all of them share an activity time, because the cursor carries the session id the order breaks ties on: a tie cannot fall between two pages and be skipped ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on activity rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L141)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` pages the same way ([validated by: pages with before and a limit, down the same newest-first order](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L62)).\n- It walks a tie exactly once too, through the same cursor ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on updatedAt rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L127)).\n- A list is at most 200 summaries however many are asked for, and 50 when none is asked for, so no caller can ask for an unbounded page ([validated by: answers at most two hundred conversations however many are asked for, and fifty when none is](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L94)).\n- That limit bounds the rows answered, not the rows the database reads to answer them: on `MongoSessionStore` the work is bounded by the `{userId: 1, updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` index `docs/session-stores.md` prescribes, and under the two-key form Mongo sorts the user's whole history before applying the limit ([validated by: needs the three-key index to answer without sorting the whole history, which the two-key form does not](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L192)).\n- A fractional limit is floored rather than refused, since a slip in a limit is not a reason to deny a user their history ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n- A negative limit, and one that is not a usable number, are read as no limit given at all rather than as a limit of none: handing a user an empty history for a typo is the worse reading ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n- Only a limit of exactly `0` answers no conversations ([validated by: answers nothing only for a limit of exactly none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L116)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` answers a limit of `0` without querying, because MongoDB reads `limit: 0` as no limit at all and would otherwise answer with every conversation the filter matches ([validated by: answers a limit of none without asking the database, which reads a limit of zero as no limit at all](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L143)).\n\n## The two shipped stores answer one order\n\n- `InMemorySessionStore` and `MongoSessionStore` list the same conversations in the same order, so a consumer swapping one for the other sees the same conversation list ([validated by: answer the same order for conversations whose activity differs](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L43)).\n- They break a tie on activity the same way, by session id ([validated by: break a tie on activity the same way, by session id](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L52)).\n- They page identically through the documented call, `listFor(userId, {limit, before: rows.at(-1)})`, a page at a time until a page comes back empty ([validated by: page the same way through the documented call, two rows at a time from the last row seen](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L61)).\n\n## A cursor the caller can actually hold\n\n- A cursor's `updatedAt` may be a `Date`, an ISO string or an epoch number, so a summary that went through JSON on its way to a client and back still pages ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, and refuses one carrying no usable moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` reads such a cursor as a date before it queries, since a string compares against no stored BSON date and would quietly match none of them ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, where a string would have matched no stored date](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L150)).\n- A cursor carrying no usable moment is refused with an error naming it, rather than read as no cursor at all, which would answer the first page again and repeat rows a client has already shown ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, and refuses one carrying no usable moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n\n## A collection that cannot list\n\n- `find` is optional on `CollectionLike`, so an adapter written before conversation lists existed still satisfies the port ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n- A store built on a collection without it refuses to list, rather than reporting that the user has no conversations ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n\n## When the store cannot answer\n\n- A store whose collection fails rejects rather than answering a partial or empty list: what to show a user who may have conversations is the caller's decision, and an empty history is not a safe guess ([validated by: rejects rather than answering a partial list when the collection fails](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L225)).\n\n## Over the WebSocket protocol\n\n- A client sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit?, before?}` and receives `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` for the socket's authenticated user, with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings and any client-supplied `userId` ignored ([validated by: answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L93)).\n- A store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}`, and a throwing `listFor` logs an error on the `ws` category and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L134)).\n- The validator accepts an optional non-negative integer `limit` and an optional `before` cursor whose `sessionId` is 1–128 characters and whose `updatedAt` parses as a valid timestamp, rejecting any other `list_sessions` payload with `INVALID_MESSAGE` without calling `listFor` ([validated by: accepts list_sessions with optional limit and before, strips unknown fields, and rejects malformed options](../../src/transport/ws/validation.test.ts#L24), [validated by: accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L163)).","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_6a5a4dcd939947fdb69a1b24","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{\n  // Keyed by session, not socket: a resumed session can be open on more than one (specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md).\n  const lock = new PerSessionLock();\n  return function handleMessage(\n answerInTurn(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator,\n  validation: ValidationResult,\n  signal: AbortSignal | undefined\n): Promise<void> {\n  // Its socket closed while it waited: nobody is left to read the answer, and a session's last close took its credentials.\n  if (signal?.aborted || ws.readyState === WebSocket.CLOSING || ws.readyState === WebSocket.CLOSED) {\n    log.info('message', 'queued message dropped: its socket closed', {sessionId: session.sessionId});\n    return;\n  }\n  const startedAt = Date.now();\n  try {\n    await wsErrorHandler(ws, () => answerUserMessage(ws, session, orchestrator, validation, signal));\n  } finally {\n    endTurn(ws, session, signal, startedAt);\n  }\n}\n\n// A turn whose socket closed is abandoned rather than ended: nobody is left to read a terminal frame.\nfunction endTurn(ws: WebSocket, session: ChatSession, signal: AbortSignal | undefined, startedAt: number): void {\n  if (signal?.aborted) {\n    log.info('message', 'turn abandoned: its socket closed', {\n      sessionId: session.sessionId,\n      elapsedMs: Date.now() - startedAt,\n    });\n    return;\n  }\n  sendStreamEnd(ws);\n}\n\nasync function answerUserMessage(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator,\n  validation: ValidationResult,\n  signal: AbortSignal | 'validation failed', {error: validation.error});\n    sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.INVALID_MESSAGE, validation.error);\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const message = validation.data;\n  if (message.type === ErrorCodes.RATE_LIMITED, 'AI service is busy, please try again');\n      return;\n    }\n    sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.SERVER_ERROR, 'Failed to process message');\n  }\n}\n\nasync function handleUserMessage(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator,\n  content: string,\n  signal: AbortSignal | undefined\n): Promise<void> {\n  log.info('message', 'user '/hal';\n\n  const wss = new WebSocketServer({\n    noServer: true,\n    handleProtocols: selectSubprotocol,\n  });\n\n  const handleMessage = createMessageHandler(options.orchestrator);\n  const examplePrompts = options.toolRegistry?.getExamplePrompts() ?? [];\n\n  const deps = {\n    wsAuth: options.wsAuth,\n    sessionStore: options.sessionStore,\n    handleMessage,\n    basePath,\n    onConnect: options.onConnect,\n    onDisconnect: options.onDisconnect,\n    resume: options.resume,\n  };\n\n  const handleUpgrade = createUpgradeHandler(wss, deps);\n  const handleConnection = createConnectionHandler(deps, examplePrompts);\n\n  const server = http.createServer(options.app);\n\n  server.on('upgrade', (request, socket, head) => {\n    handleUpgrade(request, socket, head);\n  });\n\n  wss.on('connection', ws => {\n    handleConnection(ws as ExtWebSocket);\n  });\n\n  const heartbeatMs = options.heartbeatIntervalMs ?? 30_000;\n\n  const heartbeatInterval = setInterval(() => {\n    wss.clients.forEach(ws => {\n      const extWs = ws as ExtWebSocket;\n      if (!extWs.isAlive) {\n        extWs.terminate();\n        return;\n      }\n      extWs.isAlive = false;\n      extWs.ping();\n    });\n  }, heartbeatMs);\n\n  // The listening socket should hold the process open, not the heartbeat: an engine never started must not.\n  heartbeatInterval.unref();\n\n  wss.on('close', () => clearInterval(heartbeatInterval));\n\n  return {\n    server,\n    wss,\n    start: (port?: number) =>\n      new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n        // Refused before the handlers are touched: `listen` throws on a running server, and the swap below stripped its handler.\n        if (server.listening) {\n          reject(new Error('HAL Engine is already started'));\n          return;\n        }\n\n        // ?? not ||, so a configured port 0 means \"let the OS choose\" rather than 8086.\n        const p = port ?? options.port ?? (Number(process.env.PORT) || 8086);\n\n        // Without this an EADDRINUSE settles nothing and takes the process down as an unhandled event.\n        const onError = (error: Error) => reject(error);\n        server.once('error', onError);\n\n        // A listener left from a previous start would report this bind failure as a running server breaking.\n        server.removeListener('error', logLateError);\n\n        server.listen(p, () => {\n          server.removeListener('error', onError);\n\n          // Past the listen window nothing is listening, and an 'error' with no handler ends the process.\n          server.on('error', logLateError);\n\n          // The bound port, not the requested one: a configured 0 means the OS chose it.\n          log.info('server', 'HAL Engine started', {port: boundPort(server, p)});\n          resolve();\n        });\n      }),\n    stop: () =>\n      new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n        wss.clients.forEach(ws => ws.close(1001, 'Server shutting down'));\n        wss.close();\n        clearInterval(heartbeatInterval);\n\n        // Nothing to close after a refused start or a second stop: `close` would reject for a server that never ran.\n        if (!server.listening) {\n          resolve();\n          return;\n        }\n        server.close(err => (err ? reject(err) : resolve()));\n      }),\n  };\n}\n\n// A running server's error is a condition to report, not a reason to exit; the consumer decides what to do.\nfunction logLateError(error: Error): void {\n  log.error('server', 'server error after start', {error: error.message});\n}\n\nfunction boundPort(server: http.Server, requested: number): number {\n  const address = server.address();\n  return typeof address === 'object' && address !== null ? address.port : requested;\n}\n","numLines":145,"startLine":1,"totalLines":145}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_7a0d689492fa423587717721","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

SessionResumeOptions;\n44\t}\n45\texport function createUpgradeHandler(wss: WebSocketServer, deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps) {\n46\t  return function handleUpgrade(request: IncomingMessage, socket: Duplex, head: Buffer): void {\n47\t    // Nothing may throw out of this listener: the `upgrade` event has no catch above it, so a throw ends the process.\n48\t    if (!request.headers.host || !isValidWsPath(request.url || '', deps.basePath)) {\n49\t      rejectSocket(socket, '400 Bad Request');\n50\t      return;\n51\t    }\n52\t\n53\t    authenticate(deps.wsAuth, request)\n54\t => {\n61\t          const extWs = ws as ExtWebSocket;\n62\t          extWs.userId = user.id;\n63\t          extWs.workspaceId = user['workspaceId'] as string | number | undefined;\n64\t          extWs.authHeaders = {\n65\t            cookie: request.headers.cookie,\n66\t            authorization: request.headers.authorization || bearerFromWebSocketProtocol(request),\n67\t            host: (request.headers['x-forwarded-host'] as string | undefined) ?? request.headers.host,\n68\t          };\n69\t          extWs.isAlive = true;\n70\t          if (deps.resume?.enabled) {\n71\t            extWs.requestedSessionId = sessionIdFromUpgrade(request.url || '', deps.basePath);\n72\t            extWs.startNewSession = newSessionRequested(request.url || '', deps.basePath);\n73\t          }\n74\t          wss.emit('connection', extWs, request);\n75\t        });\n76\t      })\n77\t      .catch((error: unknown) => {\n78\t        // The type alone: an authenticator's message can carry the Server Error');\n81\t      });\n82\t  };\n83\t}\n84\t\n85\t// Async, so a synchronous throw becomes a rejection (answered 500) and a user returned without a promise still resolves.\n86\tasync function ExtWebSocket): Promise<void> {\n111\t  // A requested id is never adopted for a new session: that would be session fixation.\n112\t  let sessionId = uuidv4();\n113\t  const state = {closed: false, abandons the turn in flight and every message queued behind it.\n116\t  const connection = new AbortController();\n117\t\n118\t  ws.on('error', (error: Error) => {\n119\t    log.error('ws', 'connection error', {sessionId, error: error.message});\n120\t  });\n121\t\n122\t  ws.on('pong', () => {\n123\t    ws.isAlive = true;\n124\t  });\n125\t\n126\t  ws.on('close', () => {\n127\t    // buffered, not dropped.\n135\t  ws.pause();\n136\t\n137\t  const outcome = await resumableSession(deps.sessionStore, ws, deps.resume);\n138\t  const resumed = outcome.session;\n139\t  if (resumed) sessionId = resumed.sessionId;\n140\t  const session = resumed ?? (await createSession(deps, sessionId, ws));\n141\t  state.settled = true;\n142\t\n143\t  if (session === undefined) {\n144\t    // Resumed before closing: ws.close() on a paused socket waits for a close frame it can never read.\n145\t    ws.resume();\n146\t    ws.close(1011, 'Session store unavailable');\n147\t    return;\n148\t  }\n149\t\n150\t  // A new session is this socket's from the start; a resumed one only once this socket is known to be open.\n151\t  if (!resumed) join(session, ws);\n152\t\n153\t  if (state.closed) {\n154\t    // Held first: a store that implements no evict userId: ws.userId});\n166\t\n167\t  const connected: ConnectedMessage = {\n168\t    type: 'connected',\n169\t    sessionId,\n170\t    message: 'Connected to HAL Engine',\n171\t    examplePrompts,\n172\t    ...resumeFields(deps.resume, outcome),\n173\t  };\n174\t  // A socket that died between the check above and this frame must not leave the session it was created for behind.\n175\t  try {\n176\t    ws.send(JSON.stringify(connected));\n177\t    if (resumed) replayEntries(ws, resumed);\n178\t  } catch (error) {\n179\t    log.error('ws', 'connected frame failed', 'Connection setup failed');\n184\t    return;\n185\t  }\n186\t\n187\t  state.delivered = true;\n188\t\n189\t  // Deferred, not inline: a synchronous throw in the `connection` listener corrupts an already-upgraded socket.\n190\t\n191\t  // A microtask, not setImmediate: it drains before the loop delivers any inbound frame on this socket.\n192\t  queueMicrotask(() =>\n193\t    runHook('onConnect', sessionId, () => deps.onConnect?.(session, {resumed: resumed !== undefined}))\n194\t  );\n195\t\n196\t  ws.on('message', (frame: Buffer | string) => {\n197\t    const parsed = {ConnectInfo, SessionResumeOptions} from './sessionResume.js';\nimport {log} from '../../shared/logger.js';\n\nexport interface ExtWebSocket extends WebSocket {\n  isAlive: boolean;\n  userId: string boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface ConnectionHandlerDeps {\n  wsAuth: WsAuthenticator;\n  sessionStore: SessionStore;\n  /** `signal` is the connection's own, aborted when its socket closes (specs/hal-engine-abandon-on-close/spec.md). */\n  handleMessage: (\n    ws: WebSocket,\n    session: import('../../types/session.js').ChatSession,\n    rawMessage: unknown,\n    signal?: AbortSignal\n  ) => Promise<void>;\n  basePath: string;\n  onConnect?: (session: import('../../types/session.js').ChatSession, connection: ConnectInfo) => void | Promise<void>;\n  onDisconnect?: (sessionId: string) => void | Promise<void>;\n  resume?: SessionResumeOptions;\n}\nexport function createUpgradeHandler(wss: WebSocketServer, deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps) {\n  return function handleUpgrade(request: IncomingMessage, socket: Duplex, head: Buffer): void {\n    // Nothing may throw out of this listener: the `upgrade` event has no catch above it, so a throw ends the process.\n    if (!request.headers.host || !isValidWsPath(request.url || '', deps.basePath)) {\n      rejectSocket(socket, '400 Bad Request');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    authenticate(deps.wsAuth, request)\n      .then(user => {\n        if (!user) {\n          rejectSocket(socket, '401 Unauthorized');\n          return;\n        }\n\n        wss.handleUpgrade(request, socket, head, ws => {\n          const extWs = ws as ExtWebSocket;\n          extWs.userId = user.id;\n          extWs.workspaceId = user['workspaceId'] as string | number | undefined;\n          extWs.authHeaders = {\n            cookie: request.headers.cookie,\n            authorization: request.headers.authorization || bearerFromWebSocketProtocol(request),\n            host: (request.headers['x-forwarded-host'] as string | undefined) ?? request.headers.host,\n          };\n          extWs.isAlive = true;\n          if (deps.resume?.enabled) {\n            extWs.requestedSessionId = sessionIdFromUpgrade(request.url || '', deps.basePath);\n            extWs.startNewSession = newSessionRequested(request.url || '', deps.basePath);\n          }\n          wss.emit('connection', extWs, request);\n        });\n      })\n      .catch((error: unknown) => {\n        // The type alone: an authenticator's message can carry the credential it was checking.\n        log.error('ws', 'authenticator failed', {errorType: error instanceof Error ? error.name : typeof error});\n        rejectSocket(socket, '500 Internal Server Error');\n      });\n  };\n}\n\n// Async, so a synchronous throw becomes a rejection (answered 500) and a user returned without a promise still resolves.\nasync function authenticate(wsAuth: WsAuthenticator, request: IncomingMessage): Promise<AuthenticatedUser | null> {\n  return wsAuth(request);\n}\n\nfunction bearerFromWebSocketProtocol(req: IncomingMessage): string | undefined {\n  const token = credentialFromSubprotocol(req.headers['sec-websocket-protocol']);\n  return token ? `Bearer ${token}` : undefined;\n}\n\nexport function createConnectionHandler(deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps, examplePrompts: string[]) {\n  return function handleConnection(ws: ExtWebSocket): void {\n    // The listener stays synchronous: an async one rejects into the emitter, and node ends the process on that.\n    openSession(deps, examplePrompts, ws).catch((error: unknown) => {\n      log.error('ws', 'connection setup failed', {error: messageOf(error)});\n      // Resumed before closing: a paused socket never reads the close frame it would be waiting for.\n      ws.resume();\n      ws.close(1011, 'Connection setup failed');\n    });\n  };\n}\n\n// The sockets open on each session, oldest first: a resumed session can be open on more than one at once.\nconst openSockets = new WeakMap<ChatSession, ExtWebSocket[]>();\n\nasync function openSession(deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps, examplePrompts: string[], ws: ExtWebSocket): Promise<void> {\n  // A requested id is never adopted for a new session: that would be session fixation.\n  let sessionId = uuidv4();\n  const state = {closed: false, settled: false, notified: false, delivered: false};\n  const held: {session?: ChatSession; socket: ExtWebSocket} = {socket: ws};\n  // One per connection, not per message or session: a close abandons the turn in flight and every message queued behind it.\n  const connection = new AbortController();\n\n  ws.on('error', (error: Error) => {\n    log.error('ws', 'connection error', {sessionId, error: error.message});\n  });\n\n  ws.on('pong', () => {\n    ws.isAlive = true;\n 'disconnected', {sessionId});\n    if (state.settled) endSession(deps, sessionId, state, held);\n  });\n\n  // Paused across the await so a frame arriving before the message listener exists is buffered, not dropped.\n  ws.pause();\n\n  const outcome = await resumableSession(deps.sessionStore, ws, deps.resume);\n  const resumed = outcome.session;\n  if (resumed) sessionId = resumed.sessionId;\n  const session = resumed ?? (await createSession(deps, sessionId, ws));\n  state.settled = true;\n\n  if (session === undefined) {\n    // Resumed before closing: ws.close() on a paused socket waits for a close frame it can never read.\n    ws.resume();\n    ws.close(1011, 'Session store unavailable');\n    return;\n  }\n\n  // A new session is this socket's from the start; a resumed one only once this socket is known to be open.\n  if (!resumed) join(session, ws);\n\n  if (state.closed) {\n    // Held first: a store that implements no evict still holds this session, and it carries the caller's credentials.\n    held.session = session;\n    await evictUnlessResumed(deps, sessionId, resumed);\n    endSession(deps, sessionId, state, held);\n    ws.resume();\n    return;\n  }\n\n  if (resumed) join(resumed, ws);\n  held.session = session;\n\n  log.info('ws', 'connected', {sessionId, userId: ws.userId});\n\n  const connected: ConnectedMessage = {\n    type: 'connected',\n    sessionId,\n    message: 'Connected to HAL Engine',\n    examplePrompts,\n    ...resumeFields(deps.resume, outcome),\n  };\n  // A socket that died between the check above and this frame must not leave the session it was created for behind.\n  try {\n    ws.send(JSON.stringify(connected));\n    if (resumed) replayEntries(ws, resumed);\n  } catch (error) {\n    log.error('ws', 'connected frame failed', {sessionId, error: messageOf(error)});\n    await evictUnlessResumed(deps, sessionId, resumed);\n    endSession(deps, sessionId, state, held);\n    ws.resume();\n    ws.close(1011, 'Connection setup failed');\n    return;\n  }\n\n  state.delivered = true;\n\n  // Deferred, not inline: a synchronous throw in the `connection` listener corrupts an already-upgraded socket.\n\n  // A microtask, not setImmediate: it drains before the loop delivers any inbound frame on this socket.\n  queueMicrotask(() =>\n    runHook('onConnect', sessionId, () => deps.onConnect?.(session, {resumed: resumed !== undefined}))\n  );\n\n  ws.on('message', (frame: Buffer | string) => {\n    const parsed = parseWsData(frame);\n    if (parsed === null) {\n      sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.INVALID_FORMAT, 'Invalid JSON');\n      return;\n    }\n    log.info('ws', 'message received', {sessionId, type: (parsed as Record<string, unknown>).type as string});\n    deps.handleMessage(ws, session, parsed, connection.signal);\n  });\n\n  ws.resume();\n}\n\n// Joined as the newest socket on the session, which carries this upgrade's credentials from here on.\nfunction join(session: ChatSession, ws: ExtWebSocket): void {\n  openSockets.set(session, [...(openSockets.get(session) ?? []), ws]);\n  session.authHeaders = ws.authHeaders;\n}\n\n// `undefined` rather than a throw: one store failure closes one socket instead of ending the process.\nasync function createSession(\n  deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps,\n  sessionId: string,\n  ws: ExtWebSocket\n): Promise<ChatSession | undefined> {\n  try {\n    return await deps.sessionStore.create(sessionId, ws.userId, {\n      authHeaders: ws.authHeaders,\n      workspaceId: ws.workspaceId,\n    });\n  } catch (error) {\n    log.error('ws', 'session create failed', {userId: ws.userId, error: messageOf(error)});\n    sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.SERVER_ERROR, 'Could not start a session');\n    return undefined;\n  }\n}\n\n// The close path erases nothing: the conversation outlives its socket, and `onDisconnect` is the consumer's seam.\nfunction endSession(\n  deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps,\n  sessionId: string,\n  state: {notified: boolean; delivered: boolean},\n  held: {session?: ChatSession; socket: ExtWebSocket}\n): void {\n  if (state.notified) return;\n  state.notified = true;\n\n  if (held.session) leave(held.session, held.socket);\n\n  // Only for a session the consumer was actually handed: onDisconnect is the other half of onConnect, not of a socket.\n  if (!state.delivered) return;\n\n  runHook('onDisconnect', sessionId, () => deps.onDisconnect?.(sessionId));\n}\n\n// The newest socket still open lends the session its credentials; with none left, nothing keeps them or a closed socket.\nfunction leave(session: ChatSession, ws: ExtWebSocket): void {\n  const open = openSockets.get(session) ?? a miss, a store failure and a not-yours all read as no resume.\nexport async function resumableSession(\n  store: SessionStore,\n  requester: Requester,\n  options?: SessionResumeOptions\n): Promise<ResumeOutcome> {\n  const found = await storedSession(store, requester, options);\n  if (found === undefined) return {};\n  if (found.status === 'active' && isOwnedBy(found, requester)) return {session: found.session};\n  // The latest-session default names no id, so there is no failure to report.\n  if (requester.requestedSessionId === undefined) return {};\n  return {failure: failureOf(found, requester)};\n}\n\nasync function storedSession(\n  store: SessionStore,\n  requester: Requester,\n  options: SessionResumeOptions | undefined\n): Promise<SessionLookup | undefined> {\n  try {\n    return await lookUp(store, requester, options);\n  } catch (error) {\n    const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);\n    log.error('ws', 'session lookup failed', {userId: requester.userId, error: reason});\n    return {status: 'missing'};\n  }\n}\n\n// A named id first; with none, the user's latest session, unless resume asks for none or the client asked for a new one.\nasync function lookUp(\n  store: SessionStore,\n  {requestedSessionId, startNewSession, userId}: Requester,\n  options: SessionResumeOptions | undefined\n): Promise<SessionLookup | undefined> {\n  if (requestedSessionId !== undefined) return named(store, requestedSessionId);\n  if (!options?.enabled || !options.latest || startNewSession) return undefined;\n  return asLookup(await store.latestFor?.(userId));\n}\n\n// One read per attempt: the store's lookup when it has one, else its get, which can only tell active from missing.\nasync function named(store: SessionStore, sessionId: string): Promise<SessionLookup> {\n  if (store.lookup) return store.lookup(sessionId);\n  return asLookup(await store.get(sessionId));\n}\n\nfunction asLookup(session: ChatSession | undefined): SessionLookup {\n  return session === undefined ? {status: 'missing'} : {status: 'active', session};\n}\n\n// `expired` tells the owner their session aged out; told to anyone else, it would reveal that the id exists.\nfunction failureOf(found: SessionLookup, requester: Requester): ResumeFailure {\n  return found.status === 'expired' && isOwnedBy(found, requester) ? 'expired' : 'unknown';\n}\n\nfunction isOwnedBy(found: Exclude<SessionLookup, {status: 'missing'}>, {userId}: Requester): boolean {\n  const owner = found.status === 'active' ? found.session.userId : found.userId;\n  return String(owner) === String(userId);\n}\n\n// Absent when resume is off, so a connected frame is byte-for-byte what it was before resume existed.\nexport function resumeFields(\n  options: SessionResumeOptions | undefined,\n  {session, failure}: ResumeOutcome\n): Pick<ConnectedMessage, 'resumed' | 'entryCount' | 'resumeFailure'> {\n  if (!options?.enabled) return {};\n  if (session) return {resumed: true, entryCount: session.entries.length};\n  return failure === undefined ? {resumed: false} : {resumed: false, resumeFailure: failure};\n}\n\n// A suppressed entry is replayed as a skip: the client sees the conversation it saw live, never the text a tool hid.\nexport function replayEntries(ws: WebSocket, session: ChatSession): void {\n  session.entries.forEach((entry, index) => replayEntry(ws, index, entry));\n}\n\nfunction replayEntry(ws: WebSocket, index: number, entry: SessionEntry): void {\n  if ('suppressed' in entry && entry.suppressed) {\n    sendSkip(ws, index);\n    return;\n  }\n  // Its turn streams to the socket that started it, so this client is shown it cut off rather than waiting on it.\n  if ('isStreaming' in entry && entry.isStreaming) {\n    sendUpsert(ws, index, {...entry, isStreaming: false, truncated: true});\n    return;\n  }\n  sendUpsert(ws, index, entry);\n}\n","numLines":121,"startLine":1,"totalLines":121}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_4144f68381dc4c11abfab3c0","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

===\nci.yml\nguard-main-pushes.yml\nlore-ingest.yml\nlore-trace-impact.yml\npublish.yml\n=== ci.yml ===\nname: CI\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n  push:\n    branches: [main]\n  # Manual runs: re-checking a branch against a moved main, or confirming a gate after\n  # changing one, without pushing an empty commit.\n  workflow_dispatch:\n  # An advisory published after a merge is invisible until someone opens a pull request, and this\n  # repository can go days without one. Monday 07:00 UTC; only `build-chain` answers it.\n  schedule:\n    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'\n\n# Every job here only reads the checkout; the repo default is write.\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\n# A newer push to the same branch supersedes an in-flight run. main is exempt:\n# every commit there should have its own recorded result.\nconcurrency:\n  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}\n  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}\n\njobs:\n  verify:\n    name: Verify\n    # The scheduled run exists for the dependency audit; re-running the suite on an unchanged\n    # tree every Monday would report nothing new.\n    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n          # Full history, not for this job but for the spec anchor check below:\n          # it resolves cited content from\n          # origin/main, which a shallow clone cannot serve.\n          fetch-depth: 0\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      # --ignore-scripts so `prepare` does not build on install: what a lifecycle script\n      # runs is out of this workflow's control, and the Build step below is where a broken\n      # compile should be reported. Type check catches it earlier still.\n      - name: Install\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Every `npm run` step below is one link of the `verify` script in\n      # package.json, in the same order - scripts/verify-script.test.ts holds\n      # the two together - and kept as separate steps so a red run names the\n      # gate that failed rather than a single opaque command.\n      - name: Type check\n        run: npm run typecheck\n\n      # example/ is outside tsconfig.json's rootDir, so nothing checked the one\n      # file the README and the guide are written against.\n      - name: Type check the example\n        run: npm run typecheck:example\n\n      - name: Lint (--max-warnings 0)\n        run: npm run eslint\n\n      # Reports, never blocks. The one rule it runs is `warn`, so the step exits\n      # 0 on its own and carries no continue-on-error: a non-zero exit here now\n      # means the config itself broke, and that should fail. Resolves content at origin/main, which the\n      # fetch-depth: 0 above exists to provide. A red check is fixed by running\n      # `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` and committing the result.\n      - name: Spec anchor check\n        run: node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main\n\n      # A citation counts as coverage only in its statement's trailing\n      # parenthetical; one written mid-statement is dropped by the Lore job in silence,\n      # so the spec reads as cited while its coverage is zero. A red check is\n      # fixed by moving the link to the end of its statement, never by deleting\n      # it (AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links).\n      # Every fenced typescript block in the three documented files is generated\n      # from source; hand transcription is what produced the defects this catches.\n      - name: Documented code blocks\n        run: npm run docs:check\n\n      # Three rules that held only because somebody remembered them: a path in prose that resolves,\n      # a spike that says it is a spike, and an example region inside the EU.\n      - name: Documented paths resolve\n        run: npm run docs:check-paths\n\n      - name: Spike documents carry a status block\n        run: npm run docs:check-spikes\n\n      - name: Documented regions\n        run: npm run check:regions\n\n      # A line number is a derived pointer; the name is what the author cited. This catches a citation\n      # whose line moved under it, which no baseline comparison can see on a branch that edits the spec.\n      - name: Spec citations name their test\n        run: npm run spec:names\n\n      - name: Spec link placement\n        run: npm run check:spec-links\n\n      # Lead paragraphs and a spec's status-vs-coverage are ESLint's job; the\n      # one verdict a `files` glob cannot express - that an ADR's frontmatter\n      # status parses, without holding the ADR to the coverage tier - is this\n      # script's. `check:spec-status -- --coverage` lists unlinked statements\n      # and never gates.\n      - name: Spec status\n        run: npm run check:spec-status\n\n      # A release note and a commit subject have different readers, so this is a\n      # file the author writes rather than something derived from the log. It needs the tree installed but nothing built, so it\n  # skips `prepare` with --ignore-scripts.\n  build-chain:\n    name: Build chain\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      - name: Install (no build)\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Full tree, dev included: those packages are what a runner installs\n      # before building dist/, and the release workflow signs what it produces.\n      - name: Audit (high and above)\n        run: npm run check:audit\n\n      # A tag is a mutable pointer its owner can repoint under a job that holds\n      # repository credentials.\n      - name: Action pins\n        run: npm run check:action-pins\n\n  # Its own job because it is the only check that exercises the package as a\n  # consumer receives it - packed, installed outside this tree, with no optional\n  # peer present. Everything else here tests the source in place, where every\n  # dependency is already installed and every one of these failures is invisible.\n  smoke:\n    name: Smoke (packed tarball)\n    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n        with:\n          node-version: '22'\n          cache: npm\n\n      - name: Install (no build)\n        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n\n      # Explicit, rather than relying on `npm pack` to trigger `prepare`: a build failure should be\n      # reported by a step named Build, not as a confusing pack error inside the smoke script.\n      - name: Build\n        run: npm run build\n\n      # Two variants, two jobs' worth of signal in one: `bare` is a mock-provider consumer with no\n      # optional peer, `full` is a Bedrock or Vertex consumer with both. They fail differently and\n      # separate steps name which consumer is broken.\n      - name: Smoke (no optional peer)\n        run: npm run smoke -- bare\n\n      - name: Smoke (both optional peers)\n        run: npm run smoke -- full","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ca3f5c97-de01-4300-9033-5ccb9a3fe27e","uuid":"e9b2cc0a-5e7e-4056-91cc-f23fa2e96aad","timestamp":"2026-11-07T08:04:44.494Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"        run: npm run lint:backlog\n\n      - name: Format check\n        run: npm run prettier:check\n\n      # Runs the whole suite and fails it on the committed coverage floor in\n      # jest.config.js, so this is the test gate rather than an extra pass.\n      - name: Test (with coverage floor)\n        run: npm run test:coverage\n\n      - name: Build\n        run: npm run build\n\n      # Anchors drift silently: a cited file gaining or losing lines above the\n      # cited one leaves the link pointing at different content, and the spec\n      # still reads as cited. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_3195ba5d97c64372ab0d809d","type":"tool_result","content":"      // Markdown is excluded because a doc quoting the code it documents is\n      // the intended state: README's example of createHalEngine and the\n      // interface blocks in specs/ are *supposed* to match src/. jscpd extracts\n      // fenced blocks and reports them as clones, so without this every\n      // accurate code sample is a lint error and the incentive is to let the\n      // docs drift. The same exclusion a jscpd config would carry; it lives\n      // here rather than in a .jscpd.json because the rule reads `ignore` from\n      // its own options and never from a config file.\n      're-lint/no-duplicate-code': ['error', {ignore: ['**/*.md']}],\n      're-lint/callee-below-caller': 'error',\n      're-lint/declare-near-use': 'error',\n      're-lint/default-export-matches-filename': 'error',\n      're-lint/max-boolean-operators': 'error',\n      're-lint/max-comment-lines': 'error',\n      're-lint/max-member-chain': 'error',\n      're-lint/no-closing-brace-comments': 'error',\n      're-lint/no-flag-params': 'error',\n      // INERT, kept as a placeholder. It needs type information and this config\n      // gives it none, so it reports nothing - verified with a textbook\n      // forwarding class, which it does not flag. The rule's own docs record the\n      // same finding for the same reason. It becomes a real guardrail only if\n      // this config adopts parserOptions.projectService; until then it is not\n      // one, and a clean run says nothing about forwarding classes.\n      're-lint/no-forwarding-class': 'error',\n      're-lint/no-hybrid-class': 'error',\n      're-lint/no-negative-names': 'error',\n      're-lint/no-nested-if': 'error',\n      're-lint/no-nested-loop': 'error',\n      're-lint/no-reexport-only-module': 'error',\n      're-lint/no-vague-names': 'error',\n      're-lint/prefer-early-return': 'error',\n      're-lint/prefer-polymorphism': 'error',\n      're-lint/require-fetch-timeout': 'error',\n      'no-console': 'error',\n      // Providers are loaded lazily so that selecting one never forces its SDK\n      // on consumers of the others, and the factories doing it are synchronous\n      // (`createProvider`, `createBedrockProvider`) - dynamic `import()` would\n      // make them async, which is a breaking API change. The rule stays on and\n      // still rejects every other `require()`; only these paths are permitted.\n      '@typescript-eslint/no-require-imports': [\n        'error',\n        {allow: ['^\\\\./(bedrock|vertex|openai|anthropic|mock)/index\\\\.js$', '^@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime$']},\n      ],\n    },\n  },\n  // Rules that only make sense on a test file.\n  {\n    // require-spec-link gates here: every test in\n    // the suite cites a spec statement, so the backlog it once measured is\n    // empty and an uncited new test is now a build failure rather than a\n    // number. Its statement-side mirror stays a report - see\n    // eslint.config.backlog.mjs.\n    files: ['**/*.test.ts'],\n    plugins: {'re-lint': reLint},\n    rules: {\n      're-lint/require-spec-link': 'error',\n      're-lint/max-expects': 'error',\n      're-lint/no-nondeterministic-tests': 'error',\n      're-lint/test-imports-its-subject': 'error',\n    },\n  },\n  // Every markdown link to a repo file must land. A rename sweep rewrites a\n  // dead link faithfully and the reference still reads as current, which is\n  // exactly how the spec restructure could have gone wrong.\n  {\n    files: ['**/*.md'],\n    language: 'markdown/gfm',\n    plugins: {markdown, 're-lint': reLint},\n    rules: {'re-lint/no-dead-md-links': 'error'},\n  },\n  // AGENTS.md § Spec Header Table: every spec and ADR opens with a lead\n  // paragraph, and a spec's `| Status |` row must match its test-citation\n  // coverage. ADRs are exempt from the coverage tier - asking a decision\n  // record to cite a test for every statement it makes is the wrong ask - so\n  // the second rule is scoped to specs alone.\n  {\n    files: ['specs/**/spec.md', 'adrs/*.md', 'scripts/fixtures/spec-status/**/*.md'],\n    language: 'markdown/gfm',\n    plugins: {markdown, 're-lint': reLint},\n    rules: {'re-lint/require-intro-paragraph': 'error'},\n  },\n  {\n    files: ['specs/**/spec.md', 'scripts/fixtures/spec-status/specs/**/spec.md'],\n    language: 'markdown/gfm',\n    plugins: {markdown, 're-lint': reLint},\n    // require-statement-links belongs to this pair but is deliberately absent:\n    // see eslint.config.backlog.mjs.\n    rules: {'re-lint/require-status-matches-coverage': 'error'},\n  }\n);\n=== plugin dist ===\ncli\nindex.d.mts\nindex.mjs\nrules\nvendor","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ca3f5c97-de01-4300-9033-5ccb9a3fe27e","uuid":"32dc871c-44b1-432a-9da0-81ffdc422689","timestamp":"2026-11-07T08:08:29.459Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"      // Markdown is excluded because a doc quoting the code it documents is\n      // the intended state: README's example of createHalEngine and the\n      // interface blocks in specs/ are *supposed* to match src/. jscpd extracts\n      // fenced blocks and reports them as clones, so without this every\n      // accurate code sample is a lint error and the incentive is to let the\n      // docs drift.
