Message Format\n\nAll messages are JSON objects containing a REQUIRED `type` field that identifies the message kind. Additional fields depend on the message type.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"<message_type>\",\n  ...\n}\n```\n\nA client receiving a message with an unrecognized `type` SHOULD ignore it, so that additive protocol changes do not break older clients. The server does NOT ignore unknown types: it replies with an `error` carrying code `INVALID_MESSAGE` (Section 5.6).\n\n## 4. Client-to-Server Messages\n\n### 4.1 user_message\n\nSends a user chat message. `user_message` is the only accepted type: the server previously also took `send_message`, which was removed before the first published release.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"user_message\",\n  \"content\": \"What is the weather in Berlin?\"\n}\n```\n\n| Field     | Type   | Required | Description                            |\n| --------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------- |\n| `type`    | string | Yes      | `\"user_message\"`                       |\n| `content` | string | Yes      | Message text                           |\n\nAny other field is ignored, and the validator forwards only the fields the frame defines. In particular the server does not read a `chatId` from this message: the connection already determines the session ([validated by: drops any field the frame does not define, rather than forwarding it](../../src/transport/ws/validation.test.ts#L18)).\n\nConstraints:\n\n- `content` MUST NOT be empty or whitespace-only after trimming.\n- `content` MUST NOT exceed 10,000 characters.\n- Violation of these constraints results in an `error` response with code `INVALID_MESSAGE`.\n\nOne at a time:\n\n- A session processes one `user_message` at a time, in the order the frames arrived: a frame arriving while an earlier one is still running waits, and its answer starts only after the earlier run's `stream_end` ([validated by: answers a second user_message only after the first has sent its stream_end, in the order they arrived](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L646)).\n- The waiting message's model request therefore holds the earlier answer finished, never one still streaming ([validated by: hands the second run a history whose first answer is finished, never one still streaming](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L677)).\n- A `ping` is answered at once, even while a run is pending ([validated by: answers a ping at once while a run is pending](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L695)).\n- A frame that fails validation and is not a `user_message`, such as a malformed `ping`, gets its `INVALID_MESSAGE` at once, even while a run is pending, but a `user_message` that fails validation is answered in turn, its `INVALID_MESSAGE` and `stream_end` after the run in progress, since an `error` frame names no message and would otherwise read as the running answer's ([validated by: answers an invalid ping at once but an invalid user_message in turn, after the run in progress](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L708)).\n- The reconnect flush (§ 11.3), which sends queued messages in one burst, is therefore safe: they are answered one after another, in the order the user typed them ([validated by: queues three messages sent in one tick before the handler returns, and answers them in that order](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L724)).\n- A queued message whose socket has closed by the time its turn comes is dropped, neither recorded nor answered, since nobody is left to read the answer and a session whose last socket closed has no credentials left ([validated by: drops a queued message whose socket closed before its turn, without asking the model or recording it](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L741)).\n\n### 4.2 ping\n\nApplication-level heartbeat. The server MUST respond with a `pong` message echoing the timestamp.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"ping\",\n  \"timestamp\": 1705312200000\n}\n```\n\n| Field       | Type   | Required | Description                       |\n| ----------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------- |\n| `type`      | string | Yes      | `\"ping\"`                          |\n| `timestamp` | number | Yes      | Client timestamp in milliseconds  |\n\n## 5. Server-to-Client Messages\n\n### 5.1 connected\n\nSent exactly once after a successful handshake. See Section 2.3.\n\n| Field            | Type     | Description                                            |\n| ---------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `type`           | string   | `\"connected\"`                                          |\n| `sessionId`      | string   | UUID v4 identifying the session                        |\n| `message`        | string   | Human-readable greeting                                |\n| `examplePrompts` | string[] | Example queries derived from registered tool definitions |\n| `resumed`        | boolean  | Present only with resume enabled: whether the requested conversation was rejoined |\n| `entryCount`     | number   | Present only when `resumed` is `true`: how many stored entries the replay covers, skipped ones included |\n| `resumeFailure`  | string   | Present only when the connection named an id and `resumed` is `false`: `expired` when the caller's own session aged out, `unknown` otherwise. `unknown` deliberately covers both an id the server never issued and one that is not the caller's, so the answer reveals nothing about ids that exist |\n\n### 5.2 entry_upsert\n\nCreates a new entry or replaces an existing entry at the given index. This is the primary mechanism for adding content to the conversation.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"entry_upsert\",\n  \"index\": 0,\n  \"entry\": {\n    \"role\": \"user\",\n    \"content\": \"What is the weather in Berlin?\",\n    \"timestamp\": \"2026-01-15T14:30:00Z\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n| Field   | Type         | Description                            |\n| ------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------- |\n| `type`  | string       | `\"entry_upsert\"`                       |\n| `index` | number       | Zero-based position in the entry array |\n| `entry` | SessionEntry | The entry object (see Section 6)       |\n\nSemantics:\n\n- If `index` equals the current array length, the entry is appended.\n- If `index` is within the existing array bounds, the entry at that position is replaced.\n- The client MUST NOT assume entries arrive in sequential index order during tool loops.\n- A repeat `entry_upsert` at an index the client already holds, carrying an assistant entry with empty `content`, is a **retraction**: the server is withdrawing text it already sent. See Section 5.5.\n\n### 5.3 entry_delta\n\nAppends incremental text to an existing entry's content. Only valid for entries with role `assistant` or `thinking`.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"entry_delta\",\n  \"index\": 1,\n  \"delta\": \"Berlin is \"\n}\n```\n\n| Field   | Type   | Description                                        |\n| ------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------- |\n| `type`  | string | `\"entry_delta\"`                                    |\n| `index` | number | Index of the entry to update                       |\n| `delta` | string | Text to concatenate to the entry's `content` field |\n\nSemantics:\n\n- The client MUST concatenate `delta` to `entry.content` at the given index.\n- The referenced entry MUST have `isStreaming: true`.\n- Deltas for entries with role `user` or `tool` are invalid and SHOULD be ignored.\n\n### 5.4 entry_commit\n\nMarks an entry as finalized. No further `entry_delta` messages will be sent for this index (within the current streaming sequence).\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"entry_commit\",\n  \"index\": 1\n}\n```\n\n| Field   | Type   | Description                   |\n| ------- | ------ | ----------------------------- |\n| `type`  | string | `\"entry_commit\"`              |\n| `index` | number | Index of the entry to commit  |\n\nSemantics:\n\n- The client MUST set `isStreaming` to `false` on the entry at the given index.\n- After a commit, the entry's content is considered complete and stable.\n\n### 5.5 entry_skip\n\nNotifies the client that a session entry was created on the server and will never be sent. This happens under output suppression (see [tool-responses.md](../hal-engine-tool-responses/spec.md)): the server keeps the entry so the model retains context, and the client does not need it for display ([validated by: still records a suppressed reply in the session, so history keeps it](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L211)).\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"entry_skip\",\n  \"index\": 3\n}\n```\n\n| Field   | Type   | Description                                    |\n| ------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------- |\n| `type`  | string | `\"entry_skip\"`                                 |\n| `index` | number | Server-side index of the skipped entry         |\n\nSuppression can begin before or after the server has started sending a reply, and the two cases produce different messages. This distinction is the whole of the protocol here:\n\n- An entry **opened while suppression is already active** is announced with `entry_skip` and nothing else: no `entry_upsert`, no `entry_delta`, no `entry_commit` follows it ([validated by: skips rather than upserts a segment opened after suppression](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L203)).\n- An entry **already sent before suppression began** cannot be skipped, because the client is displaying it. The server retracts it instead, by re-sending `entry_upsert` at the same index with the entry's `content` set to `\"\"`. The client renders an empty assistant entry as nothing, so the text disappears ([validated by: blanks an assistant entry that was already sent](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L180)).\n- An entry **still streaming when suppression begins** is first committed as streamed so far, with `entry_commit`, and is from then on an entry already sent: an answer is retracted as above, a thought stays as the client saw it, and whatever the model writes next opens a new entry announced with `entry_skip` ([validated by: commits and retracts an answer still open when suppression begins, and skips what follows as a new entry](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L267), [validated by: commits a thought still open when suppression begins as the client saw it, and skips what follows](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L288)).\n\n#### Limits of retraction\n\n- Only assistant entries are ever retracted; a thinking entry is never blanked, even when it was sent before suppression began ([validated by: never blanks a thinking entry, only assistant ones](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L195)).\n- Each sent entry is blanked once, so a second suppression in the same stream repeats nothing ([validated by: blanks each sent entry once, so a second suppression repeats nothing](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L229)).","numLines":180,"startLine":99,"totalLines":658}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_507e585b54d54aed9978fda3","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Server indices diverge from the client array when entries are skipped.\n284\t- The adjustment formula: for any incoming index, subtract the count of skipped indices that are less than or equal to it. The connection remains open unless the error is fatal.\n292\t\n293\t```json\n294\t{\n295\t  \"type\": \"error\",\n296\t  \"code\": \"INVALID_MESSAGE\",\n297\t  \"message\": \"Message content cannot be empty\"\n298\t}\n299\t```\n300\t\n301\t| Field     | Type   | Description              |\n302\t| --------- | ------ | ------------------------ |\n303\t| `type`    | string | `\"error\"`                |\n304\t| `code`    | string | Machine-readable code    |\n305\t| `message` | string | Human-readable detail    |\n306\t\n307\tDefined error codes:\n308\t\n309\t| Code              | Description                                                       |\n310\t| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |\n311\t| `INVALID_MESSAGE` | Message failed validation (missing fields, empty content, length) |\n312\t| `INVALID_FORMAT`  | Message body is not valid JSON                                    |\n313\t| `RATE_LIMITED`    | AI provider returned a rate limit error                           |\n314\t| `SERVER_ERROR`    | Unexpected server error during message processing                 |\n315\t\n316\tSemantics:\n317\t\n318\t- A message the server cannot parse into a known type is answered with `INVALID_MESSAGE`, and no message stream is started for it ([validated by: rejects an unparseable message and never starts a stream](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L71)).\n319\t- A rate limit reported by the AI provider is surfaced as `RATE_LIMITED`, which tells the client the same request is worth retrying ([validated by: tells the client to retry when the provider is rate limited](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L311)).\n320\t- Any other failure raised while processing a message is reported as `SERVER_ERROR` ([validated by: reports any other failure as a server error](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L320)).\n321\t\n322\t### 5.7 pong\n323\t\n324\tResponse to a client `ping`. The server MUST echo the client's timestamp without modification ([validated by: answers a ping with the timestamp it was given](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L81)).\n325\t\n326\t```json\n327\t{\n328\t  \"type\": \"pong\",\n329\t  \"timestamp\": 1705312200000\n330\t}\n331\t```\n332\t\n333\t| Field       | Type   | Description                             |\n334\t| ----------- | ------ | --------------------------------------- |\n335\t| `type`      | string | `\"pong\"`                                |\n336\t| `timestamp` | number | Echoed from the client's `ping` message |\n337\t\n338\t### 5.8 stream_end\n339\t\n340\tSignals that the server has finished processing a user message. Sent exactly once for every `user_message` the server receives, after all `entry_commit` messages have been sent, whether the run succeeded or failed.\n341\t\n342\t```json\n343\t{\n344\t  \"type\": \"stream_end\"\n345\t}\n346\t```\n347\t\n348\t| Field  | Type   | Description      |\n349\t| ------ | ------ | ---------------- |\n350\t| `type` | string | `\"stream_end\"`   |\n351\t\n352\tSemantics:\n353\t\n354\t- The server MUST send `stream_end` after every `user_message` it receives, including streams where output was suppressed (see [tool-responses.md](../hal-engine-tool-responses/spec.md)), streams that failed after an `error` frame, and a `user_message` that failed validation ([single-terminal-frame](../hal-engine-single-terminal-frame/spec.md)). The one exception is a turn whose socket closes first: it is abandoned, and nothing more is sent ([abandon-on-close](../hal-engine-abandon-on-close/spec.md)).\n355\t- `stream_end` follows every stream even after an error: a failed run sends its `error` frame first and `stream_end` last.\n356\t- An `error` frame does not by itself end a stream. It is advisory: it may concern the run in flight or an unrelated frame, such as a malformed `ping`.\n357\t- The client SHOULD use this message to clear any \"processing\" or \"loading\" indicators.\n358\t- The client MUST treat a run as complete only at `stream_end` or when the socket closes. return 0;\n  }\n\n  log.debug('stream', 'chunk', {type: chunk.type});\n  return 0;\n}\n\nfunction processChunk(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  state: StreamState,\n  parser: this.now()}},\n      {upsert: true}\n    );\n  }\n\n  /** One query, filtered on the user in the database and sorted on the index `latestFor` already needs. */\n  async listFor(userId: string | collection = await this.collection();\n    const latest = await collection.findOne({userId}, {sort: {updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}, projection: {_id: 1}});\n    return latest === null ? undefined : this.get(latest._id);\n  }\n\n  /** Erases one conversation permanently and drops it from the cache. */\n  async eraseConversation(sessionId: string): Promise<boolean> {\n    this.cache.delete(sessionId);\n    const collection = await this.collection();\n    const {deletedCount} = await collection.deleteOne({_id: sessionId});\n    return deletedCount > 0;\n  }\n\n  /** await this.collection();\n    const {deletedCount} = await collection.deleteMany({createdAt: {$lt: cutoff}});\n    return deletedCount;\n  }\n\n  /** Erases every conversation this store can see. */\n  async eraseAll(): Promise<number> {\n    this.cache.clear();\n    const collection = await this.collection();\n    const {deletedCount} = await collection.deleteMany({});\n    return deletedCount;\n  }\n\n  /** Closes the driver only when this store opened it; a supplied client stays the caller's to close. */\n  async close(): Promise<void> {\n    this.cache.clear();\n    if (this.owned === undefined) return;\n\n    await this.owned.close();\n    this.owned = undefined;\n    this.opened = undefined;\n  }\n\n  // Dropping a stale entry erases nothing: the collection is the truth and the {CollectionLike, MongoClientLike} from './mongoDriverTypes.js';\nimport type {MongoSessionDocument} from './mongoSessionDocument.js';\nimport {persistedFields, toChatSession, toSessionSummary} from './mongoSessionDocument.js';\nimport {cappedLimit, cursorAt} from '../sessionListWindow.js';\n\nconst DEFAULT_COLLECTION_NAME = 'hal_sessions';\n// Entries are left out so a page of summaries never carries a conversation out of the database.\nconst SUMMARY_FIELDS = {_id: 1, createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1, entryCount: 1} as const;\n// Eight hours, matching InMemorySessionStore: a bound on the cache in front of the collection, not a retention period.\nconst DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_MS = 8 * 60 * 60 * 1000;\n\ninterface CachedSession {\n  session: ChatSession;\n  cachedAt: number;\n}\n\ninterface SharedOptions {\n  collectionName?: string;\n  now?: () => Date;\n  maxAgeMs?: number;\n}\n\nexport type MongoSessionStoreOptions = SharedOptions &\n  (\n    | {collection: CollectionLike<MongoSessionDocument>}\n    | {client: MongoClientLike; dbName: string}\n    | {url: string; dbName: string}\n  );\n\nexport class MongoSessionStore implements SessionStore {\n  private readonly cache = new Map<string, CachedSession>();\n  private readonly options: MongoSessionStoreOptions;\n  private readonly now: () => Date;\n  private readonly maxAgeMs: number;\n  private opened: Promise<CollectionLike<MongoSessionDocument>> | undefined;\n  private owned: MongoClientLike | undefined;\n\n  constructor(options: MongoSessionStoreOptions) {\n    this.options = options;\n    this.now = options.now ?? (() => new Date());\n    this.maxAgeMs = options.maxAgeMs ?? DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_MS;\n  }\n\n  async create(sessionId: string, userId: string | number, options?: SessionCreateOptions): Promise<ChatSession> {\n    const session: ChatSession = {\n      sessionId,\n      userId,\n      entries: [],\n      authHeaders: options?.authHeaders,\n      workspaceId: options?.workspaceId,\n    };\n    const collection = await this.collection();\n    const startedAt = this.now();\n    await collection.updateOne(\n      {_id: sessionId},\n      {$set: {...persistedFields(session), createdAt: startedAt, updatedAt: startedAt}},\n      {upsert: true}\n    );\n\n    // Cached only once the write landed: a failing database would otherwise fill memory with sessions it never stored.\n    this.remember(sessionId, session);\n    return session;\n  }\n\n  async get(sessionId: string): Promise<ChatSession | undefined> {\n    const cached = this.cache.get(sessionId);\n    if (cached !== undefined && !this.hasAged(cached)) return cached.session;\n    // Dropped on a stale read too: a document erased elsewhere would otherwise leave its entry cached for good.\n    this.cache.delete(sessionId);\n\n    const collection = await this.collection();\n    const document = await collection.findOne({_id: sessionId});\n    if (document === null) return undefined;\n\n    const session = toChatSession(document);\n    this.remember(sessionId, session);\n    return session;\n  }\n\n  // The consumer's erasure primitive, which the engine never calls: it removes the document, not just the cache.\n  delete(sessionId: string): Promise<boolean> {\n    return this.eraseConversation(sessionId);\n  }\n\n  // The engine evicts only a session no client ever received, so its document holds nothing worth keeping.\n  evict(sessionId: string): Promise<boolean> {\n    return this.eraseConversation(sessionId);\n  }\n\n  async count(): Promise<number> {\n    const collection = await this.collection();\n    return collection.countDocuments();\n  }\n\n  // Empties the cache alone; eraseAll is the durable wipe, so neither can be reached by accident.\n  clear(): void {\n    this.cache.clear();\n  }\n\n  async save(session: ChatSession): Promise<void> {\n    const collection = await this.collection();\n    await collection.updateOne(\n      {_id: session.sessionId},\n      {$set: {...persistedFields(session), updatedAt: this.now()}, $setOnInsert: {createdAt: this.now()}},\n      {upsert: true}\n    );\n  }\n\n  /** One query, filtered on the user in the database and sorted on the index `latestFor` already needs. */\n  async listFor(userId: string | number, options?: SessionListOptions): Promise<SessionSummary[]> {\n    const limit = cappedLimit(options?.limit);\n    // Never issued as a query: mongo reads `limit: 0` as no limit at all, which is the opposite of what it asks for.\n    if (limit === 0) return [];\n\n    const collection = await this.collection();\n    if (collection.find === undefined) {\n      throw new StoreCannotList('The collection this store was built on implements no find, so it cannot list conversations');\n    }\n\n    const documents = await collection\n      .find(olderThan(userId, options?.before), {\n        sort: {updatedAt: -1, _id: -1},\n        limit,\n        projection: SUMMARY_FIELDS,\n      })\n      .toArray();\n    return documents.map(toSessionSummary);\n  }\n\n  /** The user's most recently saved conversation, by `updatedAt`, read through `get` so a live one is the object its running turn writes to. */\n  async latestFor(userId: string | number): Promise<ChatSession | undefined> {\n    const collection = await this.collection();\n    const latest = await collection.findOne({userId}, {sort: {updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}, projection: {_id: 1}});\n    return latest === null ? undefined : this.get(latest._id);\n  }\n\n  /** Erases one conversation permanently and drops it from the cache. */\n  async eraseConversation(sessionId: string): Promise<boolean> {\n    this.cache.delete(sessionId);\n    const collection = await this.collection();\n    const {deletedCount} = await collection.deleteOne({_id: sessionId});\n    return deletedCount > 0;\n  }\n\n  /** Erases every conversation created strictly before `cutoff`, and returns how many went. */\n  async eraseOlderThan(cutoff: Date): Promise<number> {\n    this.cache.clear();\n    const collection = await this.collection();\n    const {deletedCount} = await collection.deleteMany({createdAt: {$lt: cutoff}});\n    return deletedCount;\n  }\n\n  /** Erases every conversation this store can see. */\n  async eraseAll(): Promise<number> {\n    this.cache.clear();\n    const collection = await this.collection();\n    const {deletedCount} = await collection.deleteMany({});\n    return deletedCount;\n  }\n\n  /** Closes the driver only when this store opened it; a supplied client stays the caller's to close. */\n  async close(): Promise<void> {\n    this.cache.clear();\n    if (this.owned === undefined) return;\n\n    await this.owned.close();\n    this.owned = undefined;\n    this.opened = undefined;\n  }\n\n  // Dropping a stale entry erases nothing: the collection is the truth and the next get reloads from it.\n  private remember(sessionId: string, session: ChatSession): void {\n    for (const [cachedId, cached] of this.cache) {\n      if (!this.hasAged(cached)) break;\n      this.cache.delete(cachedId);\n    }\n    // Deleted first: `set` on an existing key keeps its old position, which would break the sweep's age order.\n    this.cache.delete(sessionId);\n    this.cache.set(sessionId, {session, cachedAt: this.now().getTime()});\n  }\n\n  private hasAged(cached: CachedSession): boolean {\n    return Number.isFinite(cached.cachedAt) && this.now().getTime() - cached.cachedAt > this.maxAgeMs;\n  }\n\n  private collection(): Promise<CollectionLike<MongoSessionDocument>> {\n    this.opened ??= this.open();\n    return this.opened;\n  }\n\n  private async open(): Promise<CollectionLike<MongoSessionDocument>> {\n    const options = this.options;\n    if ('collection' in options) return options.collection;\n\n    const name = options.collectionName ?? DEFAULT_COLLECTION_NAME;\n    if ('client' in options) return namedCollection(options.client, options.dbName, name);\n\n    // Imported here rather than at the top, so a consumer who installs no driver can still load this package.\n    const {MongoClient} = await import('mongodb');\n    const client = new MongoClient(options.url) as unknown as MongoClientLike;\n    this.owned = client;\n    return namedCollection(client, options.dbName, name);\n  }\n}\n\n// The id breaks a tie on updatedAt, so two conversations saved in the same millisecond cannot straddle a page boundary.\nfunction olderThan(userId: string | number, before: SessionCursor | undefined): Record<string, unknown> {\n  if (before === undefined) return {userId};\n  // A Date, whatever the caller held: a string compares against no BSON date, so a JSON cursor would quietly match none.\n  const updatedAt = new Date(cursorAt(before));\n  return {userId, $or: [{updatedAt: {$lt: updatedAt}}, {updatedAt, _id: {$lt: before.sessionId}}]};\n}\n\n/** Builds a MongoDB-backed session store from a collection, a client, or a connection URL. */\nexport function createMongoSessionStore(options: MongoSessionStoreOptions): MongoSessionStore {\n  return new MongoSessionStore(options);\n}\n\nfunction namedCollection(client: MongoClientLike, dbName: string, name: string): CollectionLike<MongoSessionDocument> {\n  const commits the turn's assistant entry. */\nexport const answeringOrchestrator: ChatOrchestrator = {\n  processMessage: async () => 'hi',\n  async *processMessageStream(): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n    yield {type: 'text', text: 'hi'};\n    yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n  },\n};\n\n/** Starts an engine on an ephemeral port and returns the URL a client should open. */\nexport return url;\n}\n\n/** Starts an engine with whatever a suite overrides, returning the server itself beside the URL a client should open. */\nexport async function startEngineWith(\n  options: Partial<HalServerOptions> & Pick<HalServerOptions, 'sessionStore'>\n): Promise<{url: string; hal: HalServer}> {\n  const hal = createServer({\n    app: (() => undefined) as unknown as Express,\n    wsAuth: async () => ({id: 'u1'}),\n    orchestrator: answeringOrchestrator,\n    ...options,\n  });\n  await hal.start(0);\n  servers.push(hal);\n  const {port} = hal.server.address() as JSON.parse(String(raw)) as {type: string};\n      seen.push(type);\n      if (type === until) resolve(seen);\n    });\n  });\n}\n\n/** Opens a client that asks one question the moment the socket (frame.type === 'connected') sessionId = frame.sessionId ?? '';\n  });\n  return () => sessionId;\n}\n\n/** Tears every socket and server down, so a red test reports instead of hanging the run. */\nexport async function stopEngines(): Promise<void> {\n  for (const client of clients.splice(0)) client.terminate();\n  for (const hal of servers.splice(0)) await hal.stop();\n}\n\n/** The one session a store holds, for asserting what survived a close. */\nexport async function onlySession(store: SessionStore, sessionId: string): Promise<ChatSession | undefined> {\n  return (await store.get(sessionId)) as ChatSession | undefined;\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":7,"oldLines":11,"newStart":7,"newLines":12,"lines":[" import type {ChatOrchestrator} from '../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';"," import type {MessageChunk} from '../types/ai.js';"," import type {ChatSession} from '../types/session.js';","+import {InMemorySessionStore} from '../infrastructure/stores/inMemorySessionStore.js';"," import type {SessionStore} from '../types/sessionStore.js';"," "," // Shared by the suites that need a real upgrade over a real socket, which no double can stand in for."," ","-const servers: Array<{stop: () => Promise<void>}> = [];","+const servers: HalServer[] = [];"," const clients: WebSocket[] = [];"," "," /** An orchestrator that answers once and stops, which is what commits the turn's assistant entry. */"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_f25dbf42b5da42cea58f00b8","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

'';\n  });\n  return () => sessionId;\n}\n\n/** Tears every socket and server down, so a red test reports instead of hanging the run. */\nexport async function stopEngines(): Promise<void> {\n  for (const client of clients.splice(0)) client.terminate();\n  for (const hal of servers.splice(0)) await hal.stop();\n}\n\n/** The one session a store holds, for asserting what survived a close. */\nexport async function onlySession(store: SessionStore, sessionId: string): Promise<ChatSession | undefined> {\n  return (await store.get(sessionId)) as ChatSession | undefined;\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":98,"oldLines":12,"newStart":98,"newLines":31,"lines":["   return () => sessionId;"," }"," ","-/** Tears every socket and server down, so a red test reports instead of hanging the run. */","+/** Resolves once the check holds, or half a second has passed: a close is waited for, never assumed. */","+export async function eventually(check: () => boolean): Promise<void> {","+  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 50 && !check(); attempt++) await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10));","+}","+","+/** Tears every socket and server down, each server seeing its sockets close before it stops, so a red test reports instead of hanging the run. */"," export async function stopEngines(): Promise<void> {","   for (const client of clients.splice(0)) client.terminate();","-  for (const hal of servers.splice(0)) await hal.stop();","+  for (const hal of servers.splice(0)) {","+    await eventually(() => hal.wss.clients.size === 0);","+    await hal.stop();","+  }"," }"," ","+/** A store with only the five required members, so an optional one can be added, replaced or left out per test. */","+export function delegatingTo(inner: InMemorySessionStore): SessionStore {","+  return {","+    create: (sessionId, userId, options) => inner.create(sessionId, userId, options),","+    get: sessionId => inner.get(sessionId),","+    delete: sessionId => inner.delete(sessionId),","+    count: () => inner.count(),","+    clear: () => inner.clear(),","+  };","+}","+"," /** The one session a store holds, for asserting what survived a close. */"," export async function onlySession(store: SessionStore, sessionId: string): Promise<ChatSession | undefined> {","   return (await store.get(sessionId)) as ChatSession | undefined;"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_d715792c8e534cfc84833ca2","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

servers.push(hal);\n  const {port} = hal.server.address() as AddressInfo;\n  return {auth, connects, disconnected, firstServerClose, base: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/hal/ws`};\n};\n\nconst open = (url: client.close();\n  await once(client, 'close');\n  return sessionId;\n};\n\n// A ping sent on connect is a barrier: its pong can only follow every frame the replay wrote.\nconst connectAndSettle = return {until, release: () => release()};\n};\n\n// Each stored conversation holds one user entry, sent at the given time and reading as its own id.\nconst storeWith = (conversations:   const neverIssued = await connectAndSettle(`${base}?sessionId=${NEVER_ISSUED}`);\n\n    expect({fresh: otherUser[0].sessionId !== first, otherUser: shapeOf(otherUser)}).toEqual({\n      fresh: a provider ends a tool round with no stop.\nconst suppressingMidAnswer: ChatOrchestrator = {\n  processMessage: async () => 'before after',\n  async *processMessageStream(): undefined});\n});\n\nafterAll(() => {\n  setLogger();\n});\n\n// Each server sees its sockets close before it stops, so no close is logged after the logger above is restored.\nafterEach(async () => {\n  await stopEngines();\n});\n\n// The authenticated user is read per upgrade, so one test can reconnect as someone else.\nconst startEngine = async (\n  store: SessionStore,\n  resume?: disconnected: string[] = [];\n  const {url: base, hal} = await startEngineWith({\n    sessionStore: store,\n    resume,\n    orchestrator,\n    wsAuth: async () => ({id: auth.userId}),\n    onConnect: (session, {resumed}) => void connects.push({sessionId: session.sessionId, resumed}),\n    onDisconnect: sessionId => void disconnected.push(sessionId),\n  });\n  // Resolves once the server itself has seen its first socket close, which the client's own close can precede.\n  const firstServerClose = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    hal.wss.once('connection', socket => socket.once('close', () => answered and the socket closed, returning the id the connected frame announced.\nconst firstTurn = async (base: string): Promise<string> => {\n  const client = open(base);\n  let sessionId = '';\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') sessionId = frame.sessionId ?? '';\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'user_message', content: 'hello'}));\n      if (frame.type === 'stream_end') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  client.close();\n  await once(client, 'close');\n  return sessionId;\n};\n\n// A ping sent on connect is a barrier: its pong can only follow every frame the replay wrote.\nconst connectAndSettle = async (url: string, token?: string): Promise<Frame[]> => {\n  const client = open(url, token);\n  const frames: Frame[] = [];\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      frames.push(frame);\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1}));\n      if (frame.type === 'pong') resolve();\n    });\n  });\n  return frames;\n};\n\nconst upserts = (frames: Frame[]) =>\n  frames.filter(frame => frame.type === 'entry_upsert').map(({index, entry}) => ({index, entry}));\n\nconst shapeOf = (frames: Frame[]) => ({\n  keys: Object.keys(frames[0]).sort(),\n  resumed: frames[0].resumed,\n  resumeFailure: frames[0].resumeFailure,\n  types: frames.map(frame => frame.type),\n});\n\nconst deferredRelease = () => {\n  let release = (): void => undefined;\n  const until = new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    release = resolve;\n  });\n  return {until, release: () => release()};\n};\n\n// Each stored conversation holds one user entry, sent at the given time and reading as its own id.\nconst storeWith = (conversations: Array<[sessionId: string, userId: string, sentAt: string]>): InMemorySessionStore => {\n  const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n  for (const [sessionId, userId, sentAt] of conversations) {\n    const {entries} = store.create(sessionId, userId);\n    entries.push({role: 'user', content: sessionId, timestamp: sentAt});\n  }\n  return store;\n};\n\n// A store with only the required members, so an optional one can be added, replaced or left out per test.\nconst delegatingTo = (inner: InMemorySessionStore): SessionStore => ({\n  create: (sessionId, userId, options) => inner.create(sessionId, it('never adopts a requested id as a key: one session, under the id the server minted', async () => {\n    const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    const {base} = await startEngine(store, });\n});\n\ndescribe('continuing the latest session', () => {\n  it('with latest on, rejoins the most recently active session of a user whose connect names none', async () => {\n    const store = {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_2a9380fd440148d0b10cd59f","type":"tool_result","content":"docs/getting-started.md:290:**Latest session.** A page refresh or a new tab has no id to send. With `resume: {enabled: true, latest: true}`, a connect that names no id continues the user's most recently active conversation instead of starting an empty one, and a client starts a new conversation on purpose by connecting with `?new=1`, for a \"new conversation\" button. The store decides what \"latest\" means through its optional `latestFor(userId)`: `InMemorySessionStore` goes by the newest entry, `MongoSessionStore` by `updatedAt` (create the index in [session stores](session-stores.md#latest-session)). Two tabs share the conversation but do not sync live: a reply streams to the tab that asked, and the other shows it on its next connect. \"Latest\" is keyed on the authenticated user's id, so it assumes one login per person.\ndocs/getting-started.md:292:**Why a resume failed.** When a connect names an id and is not rejoined, the `connected` frame says why in `resumeFailure`: `expired` tells the session's own owner that it aged out, and `unknown` covers every other case, an id never issued or one that is not theirs, so the answer still reveals nothing about which ids exist. Security Considerations\n641\t\n642\t- Access tokens are transmitted in the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` request header, which keeps them out of the request line and so out of a URL-based access log. They are not hidden from logging in general: an ingress or proxy that captures request headers records them, as it records an `Authorization` header, so header capture must redact `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` too.\n643\t- The server answers with the `hal.v1` marker, so the token is never written into the 101 response headers or held as the connected socket's `protocol` property. An offer without the marker is answered with no subprotocol, so no offered value is ever echoed.\n644\t- No offered subprotocol value is written to the engine's own log at any level. Every place a credential exists during a connection - request headers, the socket's and the session's `authHeaders`, and the tool context - is listed in [the subprotocol marker spec](../hal-engine-subprotocol-marker/spec.md#where-a-credential-exists).\n645\t- Message content is validated at the server boundary. Content exceeding 10,000 characters is rejected.\n646\t- The server validates all incoming messages against known types. Unrecognized types receive an `INVALID_MESSAGE` error.\n647\t\n648\t## 13. Security Considerations\n\n- Access tokens are transmitted in the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` request header, which keeps them out of the request line and so out of a URL-based access log. They are not hidden from logging in general: an ingress or proxy that captures request headers records them, as it records an `Authorization` header, so header capture must redact `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` too.\n- The server answers with the `hal.v1` marker, so the token is never written into the 101 response headers or held as the connected socket's `protocol` property. '../../shared/perSessionLock.js';\nimport type {ChatOrchestrator} from '../../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport {AIError} from '../../types/ai.js';\nimport type {MessageChunk} from '../../types/ai.js';\nimport type {SessionStore, SessionSummary, StoreCannotList} from '../../types/sessionStore.js';\nimport {\n  createUserEntry,\n  createAssistantEntry,\n  createThinkingEntry,\n  createToolEntry,\n} from '../../orchestration/entryFactories.js';\nimport {appendEntry, appendDelta, commitEntry, markTruncated} from '../../orchestration/entryMutations.js';\nimport {sendJson, sendUpsert, sendDelta, sendCommit, sendSkip, sendError, sendStreamEnd} from './sender.js';\nimport {log} from '../../shared/logger.js';\n\ninterface StreamState {\n  thinkingIndex: number | null;\n  assistantIndex: number | null;\n  suppressOutput: boolean;\n  sentAssistantIndices: number[];\n}\n\ntype StateIndexKey = 'thinkingIndex' | 'assistantIndex';\ntype EntryFactory = typeof createThinkingEntry | typeof createAssistantEntry;\n\n/** Opt-in history over the socket. GDPR: enabling it makes one user's conversation metadata reachable from the client — the list carries no conversation content, the user id comes from the connection and never from the frame, and the retention bound stays the consumer's, through the store's `maxAgeMs` and erasure methods and re-cinq/HALEngine#41. */\nexport interface HistoryOptions {\n  enabled: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface MessageHandlerOptions {\n  sessionStore?: SessionStore;\n  history?: HistoryOptions;\n}\n\nexport function createMessageHandler(orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator, options: MessageHandlerOptions = {}) {\n  // Keyed by session, not socket: a resumed session can be open on more than one (specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md).\n  const lock = new PerSessionLock();\n  return function handleMessage(\n    ws: WebSocket,\n    session: ChatSession,\n    rawMessage: unknown,\n    signal?: AbortSignal\n  ): Promise<void> {\n    const validation = validateMessage(rawMessage);\n    // Queued with no await before it, so a session's user_messages, a failed one too, are answered in arrival order.\n    if (isUserMessageFrame(rawMessage)) {\n      return lock.run(session.sessionId, () => answerInTurn(ws, session, orchestrator, validation, signal));\n    }\n    // A history request is not a turn: it mutates nothing, so it is answered beside the ping rather than queued behind a streaming answer.\n    return wsErrorHandler(ws, async () => answerFrame(ws, session, options, validation));\n  };\n}\n\n// The whole answer, an error and the stream_end included, goes out inside the lock: an error frame names no message.\nasync function answerInTurn(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator,\n  validation: ValidationResult,\n  signal: AbortSignal | undefined\n): Promise<void> {\n  // Its socket closed while it waited: nobody is left to read the answer, and a session's last close took its credentials.\n  if (signal?.aborted || ws.readyState === WebSocket.CLOSING || ws.readyState === WebSocket.CLOSED) {\n    log.info('message', 'queued message dropped: its socket closed', {sessionId: session.sessionId});\n    return;\n  }\n  const startedAt = Date.now();\n  try {\n    await wsErrorHandler(ws, () => answerUserMessage(ws, session, orchestrator, validation, signal));\n  } finally {\n    endTurn(ws, session, signal, startedAt);\n  }\n}\n\n// A turn whose socket closed is abandoned rather than ended: nobody is left to read a terminal frame.\nfunction endTurn(ws: WebSocket, session: ChatSession, signal: AbortSignal | undefined, startedAt: number): void {\n  if (signal?.aborted) {\n    log.info('message', 'turn abandoned: its socket closed', {\n      sessionId: session.sessionId,\n      elapsedMs: Date.now() - startedAt,\n    });\n    return;\n  }\n  sendStreamEnd(ws);\n}\n\nasync function answerUserMessage(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator,\n  validation: ValidationResult,\n  signal: AbortSignal | undefined\n): Promise<void> {\n  const message = validation.valid ? validation.data : undefined;\n  if (message?.type === 'user_message') return handleUserMessage(ws, session, orchestrator, message.content, signal);\n  answerFrame(ws, validation);\n}\n\nasync function answerFrame(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  options: MessageHandlerOptions,\n  validation: ValidationResult\n): Promise<void> {\n  if (!validation.valid) {\n    log.warn('message', 'validation failed', {error: validation.error});\n    sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.INVALID_MESSAGE, validation.error);\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const message = validation.data;\n  if (message.type === 'ping') handlePing(ws, message.timestamp);\n  if (message.type === 'list_conversations') await answerListConversations(ws, session, options, message);\n}\n\n// The list is always the connection's own: the user id comes from the upgrade, and the frame's own user field never reaches the store.\nasync function answerListConversations(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  options: MessageHandlerOptions,\n  message: ListConversationsMessage\n): Promise<void> {\n  if (!options.history?.enabled || !options.sessionStore) {\n    sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.UNSUPPORTED, 'Conversation history is not enabled on this server');\n    return;\n  }\n  const store = options.sessionStore;\n  if (!store.listFor) {\n    sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.UNSUPPORTED, 'The session store cannot list conversations');\n    return;\n  }\n  try {\n    // Both keys, even when undefined, so every store sees one call shape.\n    const summaries = await store.listFor(ws.userId, {limit: message.limit, before: message.before});\n    sendJson(ws, {type: 'conversation_list', conversations: summaries.map(summaryOnWire)});\n  } catch (error) {\n    // A store that refuses to list is a misconfiguration, not a failure: an empty history would read as data.\n    if (error instanceof StoreCannotList) {\n      sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.UNSUPPORTED, 'The session store cannot list conversations');\n      return;\n    }\n    log.error('ws', 'conversation list failed', {\n      sessionId: session.sessionId,\n      error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),\n    });\n    sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.SERVER_ERROR, 'Could not list conversations');\n  }\n}\n\n// A summary's dates are `Date`s in the store and ISO strings on the wire, which a `Date` does not survive `JSON.stringify` as.\nfunction summaryOnWire(summary: SessionSummary): ConversationSummary {\n  return {\n    sessionId: summary.sessionId,\n    createdAt: summary.createdAt.toISOString(),\n    updatedAt: summary.updatedAt.toISOString(),\n    entryCount: summary.entryCount,\n  };\n}\n\n// Read from the raw frame, so a user_message that fails validation still gets its stream_end.\nfunction isUserMessageFrame(rawMessage: unknown): boolean {\n  return typeof rawMessage === 'object' && rawMessage !== null && Reflect.get(rawMessage, 'type') === 'user_message';\n}\n\nasync function wsErrorHandler(ws: WebSocket, action: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {\n  try {\n    await action();\n  } catch (error) {\n    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error';\n    const code = error instanceof AIError ? error.code : 'UNKNOWN';\n    log.error('message', 'handling error', {error: message, code});\n    if (error instanceof AIError && error.code === 'RATE_LIMITED') {\n      sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.RATE_LIMITED, 'AI service is busy, please try again');\n      return;\n    }\n    sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.SERVER_ERROR, 'Failed to process message');\n  }\n}\n\nasync function handleUserMessage(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  orchestrator: ChatOrchestrator,\n  content: string,\n  signal: AbortSignal | undefined\n): Promise<void> {\n  log.info('message', 'user message received', {sessionId: session.sessionId, contentLength: content.length});\n\n  const userEntry = createUserEntry(content);\n  const userIndex = appendEntry(session, userEntry);\n  sendUpsert(ws, userIndex, userEntry);\n\n  const parser = new ThinkingTagParser();\n  const state: StreamState = {\n    thinkingIndex: null,\n    assistantIndex: null,\n    suppressOutput: false,\n    sentAssistantIndices: [],\n  };\n\n  let textChunkCount = 0;\n\n  try {\n    for await (const chunk of orchestrator.processMessageStream(session, {signal})) {\n      // Its socket closed: breaking returns the run's generator, so the run stops and its own teardown still runs.\n      if (signal?.aborted) break;\n      textChunkCount = logChunk(chunk, textChunkCount);\n      processChunk(ws, session, state, parser, chunk);\n    }\n  } finally {\n    // Anything still open here was cut short: a stop has already flushed the parser and committed every entry it opened.\n    flushHeldText(ws, session, state, parser);\n    closeCutOff(ws, session, state, 'thinkingIndex');\n    closeCutOff(ws, session, state, 'assistantIndex');\n  }\n\n  if (textChunkCount > 0) {\n    log.debug('stream', `received ${textChunkCount} text chunks`);\n  }\n  log.info('stream', 'stream completed', {suppressed: state.suppressOutput, entries: session.entries.length});\n}\n\n// Diagnostics only: counts a run of text chunks so it is logged once, not per token.\nfunction logChunk(chunk: MessageChunk, textChunkCount: number): number {\n  if (chunk.type === 'text') return textChunkCount + 1;\n\n  if (textChunkCount > 0) {\n    log.debug('stream', `received ${textChunkCount} text chunks`);\n  }\n\n  if (chunk.type === 'tool_result') {\n    log.debug('stream', 'tool_result chunk', {\n      messageCount: chunk.clientMessages.length,\n      types: chunk.clientMessages.map(m => m.type),\n    });\n    return 0;\n  }\n\n  log.debug('stream', 'chunk', {type: chunk.type});\n  return 0;\n}\n\nfunction processChunk(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  state: StreamState,\n  parser: ThinkingTagParser,\n  chunk: MessageChunk\n): void {\n  if (chunk.type === 'text') return processTextChunk(ws, session, state, parser, chunk.text);\n  if (chunk.type === 'tool_use') return processToolUseChunk(ws, session, chunk.toolCall);\n  if (chunk.type === 'tool_result') return processToolResultChunk(ws, chunk.clientMessages);\n  if (chunk.type === 'suppress_output') return processSuppressChunk(ws, session, state);\n  if (chunk.type === 'stop') return processStopChunk(ws, session, state, parser);\n}\n\nfunction processTextChunk(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  state: StreamState,\n  parser: ThinkingTagParser,\n  text: string\n): void {\n  const segments = parser.push(text);\n  for (const segment of segments) {\n    handleTextSegment(ws, session, state, segment);\n  }\n}\n\nfunction handleTextSegment(ws: WebSocket, session: ChatSession, state: StreamState, segment: ParsedSegment): void {\n  if (segment.type === 'thinking') {\n    streamSegment(ws, session, state, 'thinkingIndex', createThinkingEntry, segment.content);\n    return;\n  }\n  commitAndClear(ws, session, state, 'thinkingIndex');\n  streamSegment(ws, session, state, 'assistantIndex', createAssistantEntry, segment.content);\n}\n\nfunction streamSegment(\n  ws: WebSocket,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  state: StreamState,\n  key: StateIndexKey,\n  createEntry: EntryFactory,\n  content: string\n): void {\n  const isNew = initSegment(session, state, key, createEntry);\n  if state[key]!, content);\n  if (!state.suppressOutput) sendDelta(ws, state[key]!, content);\n}\n\n// Stored as suppressed, so a replay on resume shows the client what it saw live and not the text a tool hid.\nfunction skipSuppressed(ws: WebSocket, session: ChatSession, index: number): void {\n  markSuppressed(session, index);\n  sendSkip(ws, index);\n}\n\nfunction markSuppressed(session: ChatSession, index: number): void {\n  const entry = session.entries[index];\n  if (entry.role === 'assistant' || entry.role === 'thinking') entry.suppressed = true;\n}\n\nfunction initSegment(session: ChatSession, state: StreamState, key: StateIndexKey, createEntry: EntryFactory): boolean {\n  if (state[key] !== null) return false;\n  state[key] = appendEntry(session, createEntry());\n  return true;\n}\n\nfunction commitAndClear(ws: WebSocket, session: ChatSession, state: StreamState, key: StateIndexKey): void {\n  const index = state[key];\n  if (index === null) return;\n\n  commitEntry(session, index);\n  state[key] = null;\n\n  // Only what the client received can be retracted, and only assistant entries.\n  if (state.suppressOutput) return;\n\n  sendCommit(ws, return;\n    }\n    log.info('ws', 'message received', {sessionId, type: (parsed as Record<string, unknown>).type as string});\n    deps.handleMessage(ws, session, parsed, connection.signal);\n personal data — that a user held a conversation, and when — so it carries no conversation content, it is filtered to one user by the query rather than in application code afterwards, and the retention members satisfying the interface beside both shipped ones](../../src/infrastructure/stores/sessionStoreListSignature.test.ts#L11)).\n14\t\n15\t## The order a list answers in\n16\t\n17\t- Summaries come back most recent activity first ([validated by: answers newest activity first, headed by the very session latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L27)).\n18\t- The first summary is the session `latestFor` returns, because both read the same activity ([validated by: answers newest activity first, headed by the very session latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L27)).\n19\t- The order is total rather than merely sorted: two conversations last active in the same millisecond are ordered by session id, the larger first, which is what lets a page resume without dropping one of them ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on activity rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L141)).\n20\t- In `InMemorySessionStore` that tie-break is the list's alone: `latestFor` breaks the same tie by creation order, so for two tied conversations the head of the list and the session a resume rejoins can differ ([validated by: breaks a tie on activity by session id, where latestFor takes the session created later](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L42)).\n21\t- `MongoSessionStore` answers in order of `updatedAt`, which each `save` moves forward, and its first summary is the session its own `latestFor` returns ([validated by: answers the user's conversations newest saved first, headed by the one latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L31)).\n22\t- It breaks a tie by `_id` in both members, so there the head of the list is the session a resume updatedAt](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L161)).\n23\t\n24\t## What a summary reports\n25\t\n26\t- `InMemorySessionStore` reports the moment `create` was called, the newest entry time as the activity, and the conversation's entry count ([validated by: reports a creation time, the newest activity and the entry count of each conversation](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L53)).\n27\t- `MongoSessionStore` reports the document's `createdAt`, the `updatedAt` its last save wrote, and the counter written beside the entries ([validated by: reports the creation time, the last save and the entry count of each conversation](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L49)).\n28\t- That counter is what a save writes, so a list never reads a conversation to count one ([validated by: counts a conversation from the field a save writes beside the entries](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L95)).\n29\t- A document written before the counter existed reads as a conversation of no entries rather than failing the list, which is what the backlog documented in `docs/session-stores.md` is for ([validated by: reads a conversation saved before the counter existed as one of no entries, rather than failing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L79)).\n30\t\n31\t## Whose conversations\n32\t\n33\t- A list holds only a conversation that aged out and another user's, and answers nothing for a user with none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L65)).\n35\t- `MongoSessionStore` filters on most 200 summaries however many are asked for, and 50 when none is asked for, so no caller can ask for an unbounded page ([validated by: answers at most two hundred conversations however many are asked for, and fifty when none is](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L94)).\n45\t- That limit bounds the rows answered, not the rows the database reads to answer them: on `MongoSessionStore` the work is bounded by the `{userId: 1, updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` index `docs/session-stores.md` prescribes, and under the two-key form Mongo sorts the user's whole history before applying the limit ([validated by: needs the three-key index to answer without sorting the whole history, which the two-key form does not](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L192)).\n46\t- A fractional limit is floored rather than refused, since a slip in a limit is not a reason to deny a user their history ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n47\t- A negative limit, and one that is not a usable number, are read as no limit given at all rather than as a limit of none: handing a user an empty history for a typo is the worse reading ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n48\t- Only a limit of exactly `0` answers no conversations ([validated by: answers nothing only for a limit of exactly none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L116)).\n49\t- `MongoSessionStore` answers a limit of `0` without querying, because MongoDB reads `limit: 0` as no limit at all and would otherwise answer with every conversation the filter matches ([validated by: answers a limit of none without asking the database, which reads a limit of zero as no limit at all](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L143)).\n50\t\n51\t## The two shipped stores answer one order\n52\t\n53\t- `InMemorySessionStore` and `MongoSessionStore` list differs](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L43)).\n54\t- They break a tie on activity the same way, by session id ([validated by: break a tie on activity the same way, by session id](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L52)).\n55\t- They page identically through the documented call, `listFor(userId, {limit, before: rows.at(-1)})`, a page at a time until a page comes back empty ([validated by: page the same way through the documented call, two rows at a time from the last row seen](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L61)).\n56\t\n57\t## A cursor the caller can actually hold\n58\t\n59\t- A cursor's `updatedAt` may be a `Date`, an ISO string or an moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n60\t- `MongoSessionStore` reads such a cursor as a date before it queries, since a string compares against no stored BSON date and would quietly match none of them ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, where a string would have matched no stored date](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L150)).\n61\t- A cursor carrying no usable moment is refused with an error naming it, rather than read as no cursor at all, which would answer the first page again and repeat rows a client has already shown ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, and refuses one carrying no usable moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n62\t\n63\t## A collection that cannot list\n64\t\n65\t- `find` is optional on `CollectionLike`, so an adapter written before conversation lists existed still satisfies the port ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n66\t- A store built on a collection without it refuses to list, rather than reporting that the user has no conversations ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n67\t\n68\t## When the store cannot answer\n69\t\n70\t- A store whose collection fails rejects rather than answering a partial or empty list: what to show a user who may have conversations is the caller's decision, and an empty history is not a safe guess ([validated by: rejects rather than answering a partial list when the collection fails](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L225)).\n71\t\n72\t## Over the WebSocket protocol\n73\t\n74\t- A client sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit?, before?}` and receives `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` for the socket's authenticated user, with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings and any client-supplied `userId` ignored ([validated by: answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client `ws` category and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L134)).\n76\t- The validator accepts an optional non-negative integer `limit` and an optional `before` cursor whose `sessionId` is 1–128 characters and whose `updatedAt` parses as a valid timestamp, rejecting any other `list_sessions` payload with `INVALID_MESSAGE` without calling `listFor` ([validated by: accepts list_sessions with optional limit and before, strips unknown fields, and rejects malformed options](../../src/transport/ws/validation.test.ts#L24), [validated by: accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n\n## When the store cannot answer\n\n- A store whose collection fails rejects rather than answering a partial or empty list: what to show a user who may have conversations is the caller's decision, and an empty history is not a safe guess ([validated by: rejects rather than answering a partial list when the collection fails](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L225)).\n\n## Over the WebSocket protocol\n\n- A client sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit?, before?}` and receives `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` for the socket's authenticated user, with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings and any client-supplied `userId` ignored ([validated by: answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L93)).\n- A store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}`, and a throwing `listFor` logs an error on the `ws` category and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L134)).\n- The validator accepts an optional non-negative integer `limit` and an optional `before` cursor whose `sessionId` is 1–128 characters and whose `updatedAt` parses as a valid timestamp, rejecting any other `list_sessions` payload with `INVALID_MESSAGE` without calling `listFor` ([validated by: accepts list_sessions with optional limit and before, strips unknown fields, and rejects malformed options](../../src/transport/ws/validation.test.ts#L24), [validated by: accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L163)).\n","numLines":77,"startLine":1,"totalLines":77}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_545418bcb5aa4baf96dfd4be","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"id":"msg_20261107163626e777801f7c214107","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"glm-5.3-flash","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"call_09e2018600f5472e82da4b46","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/a57de5b927b4/workspace/target/src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts","content":"import {\n  announcedId,\n  askOnOpen,\n  connectClient,\n  deferred,\n  delegatingTo,\n  eventually,\n  onlySession,\n  startEngineWith,\n  stopEngines,\n} from './wsTestSupport.js';\nimport {InMemorySessionStore} from '../infrastructure/stores/inMemorySessionStore.js';\nimport {StoreCannotList} from '../types/sessionStore.js';\nimport type {SessionListOptions, SessionStore, SessionSummary} from '../types/sessionStore.js';\nimport type {ChatOrchestrator} from '../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport type {MessageChunk} from '../types/ai.js';\nimport type {SessionEntry} from '../types/session.js';\nimport {setLogger} from '../shared/logger.js';\n\n// Real upgrades over a real socket: what a list answers is the wire contract, and no double can observe it.\n\ninterface Frame {\n  type: string;\n  sessionId?: string;\n  resumed?: boolean;\n  entryCount?: number;\n  code?: string;\n  message?: string;\n  index?: number;\n  entry?: SessionEntry;\n  conversations?: Array<{sessionId: string; createdAt: string; updatedAt: string; entryCount: number}>;\n}\n\nconst lines: Array<{level: string; category: string; message: string; fields?: Record<string, unknown>}> = [];\nconst listen = (level: string) => (category: string, message: string, fields?: Record<string, unknown>) => {\n  lines.push({level, category, message, fields});\n};\n\nbeforeEach(() => {\n  lines.length = 0;\n  setLogger({debug: listen('debug'), info: listen('info'), warn: listen('warn'), error: listen('error')});\n});\n\nafterEach(async () => {\n  // Each server sees its sockets close before it stops, so no close lands after the logger below is restored.\n  await stopEngines();\n  setLogger();\n});\n\n// An ask sent once the handshake answers, read through a ping barrier: the pong can only follow every frame the answer wrote.\nconst askAfterConnect = async (url: string, outbound?: object): Promise<{connected: Frame; frames: Frame[]}> => {\n  const client = connectClient(url);\n  const frames: Frame[] = [];\n  let connected: Frame = {type: ''};\n  const ask = (frame: Frame): void => {\n    connected = frame;\n    if (outbound !== undefined) client.send(JSON.stringify(outbound));\n    client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1}));\n  };\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') return ask(frame);\n      if (frame.type === 'pong') return resolve();\n      frames.push(frame);\n    });\n  });\n  return {connected, frames};\n};\n\nconst codesOf = (frames: Frame[]): Array<{type: string; code?: string}> => frames.map(({type, code}) => ({type, code}));\n\nconst upserts = (frames: Frame[]): Array<{index?: number; entry?: SessionEntry}> =>\n  frames.filter(frame => frame.type === 'entry_upsert').map(({index, entry}) => ({index, entry}));\n\n/** A store whose listFor counts its asks and answers none, so a test can tell whether the store was consulted. */\nconst countingStore = (): {store: SessionStore; asks: () => number} => {\n  let asks = 0;\n  return {\n    store: {\n      ...delegatingTo(new InMemorySessionStore()),\n      listFor: () => {\n        asks += 1;\n        return [];\n      },\n    },\n    asks: () => asks,\n  };\n};\n\ndescribe('a conversation list over the WebSocket protocol', () => {\n  it('answers the connected user with ISO summaries, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId', async () => {\n    const seen: Array<{userId: string | number; options?: SessionListOptions}> = [];\n    const newestFirst: SessionSummary[] = [\n      {\n        sessionId: 's3',\n        createdAt: new Date('2026-01-03T00:00:00.000Z'),\n        updatedAt: new Date('2026-01-03T00:03:00.000Z'),\n        entryCount: 9,\n      },\n      {\n        sessionId: 's2',\n        createdAt: new Date('2026-01-02T00:00:00.000Z'),\n        updatedAt: new Date('2026-01-02T00:02:00.000Z'),\n        entryCount: 4,\n      },\n      {\n        sessionId: 's1',\n        createdAt: new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'),\n        updatedAt: new Date('2026-01-01T00:01:00.000Z'),\n        entryCount: 2,\n      },\n    ];\n    const store: SessionStore = {\n      ...delegatingTo(new InMemorySessionStore()),\n      listFor: (userId, options) => {\n        seen.push({userId, options});\n        return newestFirst;\n      },\n    };\n\n    const {frames} = await askAfterConnect((await startEngineWith({sessionStore: store})).url, {\n      type: 'list_conversations',\n      limit: 10,\n      before: {updatedAt: '2026-01-03T00:03:00.000Z', sessionId: 's3'},\n      userId: 'u2',\n    });\n\n    expect({seen, frames}).toEqual({\n      seen: [{userId: 'u1', options: {limit: 10, before: {updatedAt: '2026-01-03T00:03:00.000Z', sessionId: 's3'}}}],\n      frames: [\n        {\n          type: 'conversation_list',\n          conversations: [\n            {\n              sessionId: 's3',\n              createdAt: '2026-01-03T00:00:00.000Z',\n              updatedAt: '2026-01-03T00:03:00.000Z',\n              entryCount: 9,\n            },\n            {\n              sessionId: 's2',\n              createdAt: '2026-01-02T00:00:00.000Z',\n              updatedAt: '2026-01-02T00:02:00.000Z',\n              entryCount: 4,\n            },\n            {\n              sessionId: 's1',\n              createdAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z',\n              updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:01:00.000Z',\n              entryCount: 2,\n            },\n          ],\n        },\n      ],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('with history off or absent, answers UNSUPPORTED and never asks the store', async () => {\n    const absent = countingStore();\n    const off = countingStore();\n\n    const withoutFlag = await askAfterConnect((await startEngineWith({sessionStore: absent.store})).url, {\n      type: 'list_conversations',\n    });\n    const disabled = await askAfterConnect(\n      (await startEngineWith({sessionStore: off.store, history: {enabled: false}})).url,\n      {type: 'list_conversations'}\n    );\n\n    expect({\n      withoutFlag: codesOf(withoutFlag.frames),\n      disabled: codesOf(disabled.frames),\n      asks: [absent.asks(), off.asks()],\n    }).toEqual({\n      withoutFlag: [{type: 'error', code: 'UNSUPPORTED'}],\n      disabled: [{type: 'error', code: 'UNSUPPORTED'}],\n      asks: [0, 0],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('answers UNSUPPORTED when the store cannot list, whether listFor is absent or the store refuses', async () => {\n    const bare = (await startEngineWith({sessionStore: delegatingTo(new InMemorySessionStore())})).url;\n    const refusing = (\n      await startEngineWith({\n        sessionStore: {\n          ...delegatingTo(new InMemorySessionStore()),\n          listFor: () => Promise.reject(new StoreCannotList('this store holds conversations but cannot list them')),\n        },\n      })\n    ).url;\n\n    const withoutListFor = await askAfterConnect(bare, {type: 'list_conversations'});\n    const refused = await askAfterConnect(refusing, {type: 'list_conversations'});\n\n    expect({withoutListFor: codesOf(withoutListFor.frames), refused: codesOf(refused.frames)}).toEqual({\n      withoutListFor: [{type: 'error', code: 'UNSUPPORTED'}],\n      refused: [{type: 'error', code: 'UNSUPPORTED'}],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('answers a rejecting listFor with SERVER_ERROR on a socket left open, logging the session id without the store detail', async () => {\n    const store: SessionStore = {\n      ...delegatingTo(new InMemorySessionStore()),\n      listFor: () => Promise.reject(new Error('database offline')),\n    };\n\n    // The pong behind the error is the socket's own proof it stayed open, since askAfterConnect stops on nothing else.\n    const {connected, frames} = await askAfterConnect((await startEngineWith({sessionStore: store})).url, {\n      type: 'list_conversations',\n    });\n    const failures = lines.filter(line => line.level === 'error' && line.category === 'ws');\n\n    expect({\n      failed: frames.map(({type, code, message}) => ({\n        type,\n        code,\n        carriesStoreDetail: message?.includes('database offline'),\n      })),\n      failures,\n    }).toEqual({\n      failed: [{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR', carriesStoreDetail: false}],\n      failures: [\n        {\n          level: 'error',\n          category: 'ws',\n          message: 'conversation list failed',\n          fields: {sessionId: connected.sessionId, error: 'database offline'},\n        },\n      ],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('accepts a bare list_conversations frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor', async () => {\n    const listed = countingStore();\n    const url = (await startEngineWith({sessionStore: listed.store})).url;\n    const malformed = [\n      {type: 'list_conversations', limit: '10'},\n      {type: 'list_conversations', limit: 0},\n      {type: 'list_conversations', limit: -1},\n      {type: 'list_conversations', limit: 1.5},\n      {type: 'list_conversations', limit: 201},\n      {type: 'list_conversations', before: 'not an object'},\n      {type: 'list_conversations', before: {updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'}},\n      {type: 'list_conversations', before: {sessionId: 's1'}},\n      {type: 'list_conversations', before: {updatedAt: 'not a date', sessionId: 's1'}},\n      {type: 'list_conversations', before: {updatedAt: 1767225600000, sessionId: 's1'}},\n    ];\n\n    const codes: Array<string | undefined> = [];\n    for (const frame of malformed) {\n      const {frames} = await askAfterConnect(url, frame);\n      codes.push(frames[0]?.code);\n    }\n    const bare = await askAfterConnect(url, {type: 'list_conversations'});\n\n    expect({codes, bare: bare.frames, asks: listed.asks()}).toEqual({\n      codes: malformed.map(() => 'INVALID_MESSAGE'),\n      bare: [{type: 'conversation_list', conversations: []}],\n      asks: 1,\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('answers a list asked while a turn streams on the same session before that turn streams its end', async () => {\n    const held = deferred();\n    const midAnswer: ChatOrchestrator = {\n      processMessage: async () => 'half',\n      async *processMessageStream(): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n        yield {type: 'text', text: 'half'};\n        await held.until;\n        yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n      },\n    };\n    const store: SessionStore = {\n      ...delegatingTo(new InMemorySessionStore()),\n      listFor: () => [{sessionId: 's1', createdAt: new Date(0), updatedAt: new Date(0), entryCount: 0}],\n    };\n    const {url} = await startEngineWith({sessionStore: store, history: {enabled: true}, orchestrator: midAnswer});\n\n    const client = connectClient(url);\n    const during: string[] = [];\n    const afterRelease: string[] = [];\n    let seen = during;\n    await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n      client.on('message', raw => {\n        const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n        seen.push(frame.type);\n        if (frame.type === 'connected') return client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'user_message', content: 'hello'}));\n        if (frame.type === 'entry_delta') {\n          client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'list_conversations', limit: 5}));\n          client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1}));\n          return;\n        }\n        if (frame.type === 'pong') return resolve();\n      });\n    });\n    seen = afterRelease;\n    held.release();\n    await eventually(() => afterRelease.includes('stream_end'));\n\n    expect({during, afterRelease}).toEqual({\n      during: ['connected', 'entry_upsert', 'entry_upsert', 'entry_delta', 'conversation_list', 'pong'],\n      afterRelease: ['entry_commit', 'stream_end'],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('hands a client that reconnects with a listed id its own conversation back, resumed and replayed', async () => {\n    const store = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    const {url} = await {InMemorySessionStore} from '../infrastructure/stores/inMemorySessionStore.js';\nimport {StoreCannotList} from '../types/sessionStore.js';\nimport type {SessionListOptions, SessionStore,
